My bf who isnt celiac and basically has to change his diet because of me was raving how good it was, he wanted to keep eating more of it. Its fun to make your own toppings and add different cheeses. Ive been to gourmet gluten free pizza places and this tasted just as good for much much less. I give it 2 thumbs up and I will keep buying this product. Thanks for making a celiac girl feel like she can have pizza again!

My teenager surprised me with a gluten free pizza from Bob's Red Mill. This is the best gluten free pizza dough! It is different from a wheat gluten dough, however it looks like wheat pizza, but the ingredients are so much healthier! If you follow the instructions it will be a success! After many years with no pizza, I will now enjoy pizza again. Thank you Bob's Red Mill!
This gluten free pizza is easy to make and has an excellent flavor as pizza or bread sticks ! Love it !!

After trying several frozen and commercially-prepared gluten free pizzas, I've finally found a winner. The crust is easy to prepare, bakes perfectly every time, and tastes delicious. I like that there are two crusts per bag of mix, too. Try this if you're looking for a quick, good, gluten-free crust.
Excellent results, one bag made a thick 16" pizza.  Next time will mak a 16 and 12 inch pizza
Don't miss out on your favorite foods due to Gluten intolerance!This product makes a wonderful crust, not just pizza!

This is a great GF product, and one of the best home-made pizza crusts I have ever made. These mixes are easy to use and taste great. I make three personal pan pizzas in round cake pans instead of one large pizza. I think the crust cooks better this way. You can also make yummy garlic bread out of the mix.

I've been on a GF diet for almost 5 years.  I've tried several GF pizza crust mixes but they've all been pretty gross.  The I tried Bob's Red Mill GF Pizza Crust mix.  It is fantastic!  I ordered 1 box (which contained 4 packages) about a month ago and we've already used 3 of them.  My whole family eats it even though I'm the only one that HAS to eat GF.  I love it.  It tastes like regular pizza crust unlike all the others I've tried.

I was diagnosed two weeks ago and have been frantically trying to find replacements for some of my favorite foods.  This crust is GREAT.  I really couldn't tell that I was eating gluten free.  I was surprised since I found Bob's All Purpose flour to be completely inedible.  My husband and several friends eating with me also enjoyed it.  Ok, it is real cooking... it takes about 45 minutes from deciding "I want pizza" to being able to eat it.  But you CAN eat it and it tastes GOOD.

column9: Bob's Red Mill Gluten free pizza crust mix
column10: The crust is very tasty.  Mine turned out a little on the damp side so maybe keep a little extra gluten free flour on hand for rolling.

We've tried so many mealy, grainy, funky-tasting GF pizza crusts and weren't expecting any different from this one. Thankfully we were very wrong! The texture and taste of this crust are fantastic. No weird aftertaste, no odd graininess. Remembering to wet your hands when you pat out the dough is the only trick. Our next experiment will be to make cheese bread and stromboli with this crust. We won't buy another kind.

This is hands down the best GF pizza crust out there. I've found that if you follow the directions exactly you'll end up with a pizza crust that tastes better and has a better consistency than any you can order at any GF restaurant (in the tri-state area, at least). Also, you can make it deep dish or thin crust and the crust holds up either way. I've never come across GF pizza in any restaurant that isn't thin crust so now having the ability to have a thicker, more substantial crust is excellent. Bottom Line: if you're on a GF diet and you love pizza, buy this crust. Just a hint, the sauce you use (in any pizza) makes a huge difference in taste. I think the best sauce out there is Rao's but it can be a bit pricey ($11/bottle or plus) but you can catch it on sale at Stew Leonard's for either $7 or 2 for $12. I'm gonna' try making a calzone so I'll update regarding that once I do.

If you follow the instructions- this is great. I have three kids and a husband that can eat gluten and this is one of the few dinners where everyone actually prefers the glutenfree version. My husband included. This is the best gluten-free product/baking mix that I have found! And that's saying something; I cook a lot.

Having to be gluten free is hard enough, but life without pizza is misery!  This was such an easy product to use, worked with egg replacer just fine, had a great texture and wonderful flavor!  The directions are clear and easy to follow.  I would eat this even if I wasn't gluten free!

I was very disappointed in this product. I only bought it because the reviews sounded promising. It was gloppy, stuck to the pan terribly, had a terrible texture once cooked, and didn't resemble a pizza crust in any way. I am a very good baker and cook and never have a recipe just flop, but this was beyond my help. It did make more than one pizza crust; I'll give them that, but the crust was not worth the trouble and didn't taste good, so why would I want another one lying around? Save your money and buy a Chebe mix. They are wonderful.

column9: Not many GF places better than Bob's...
column10: I haven't had a bad batch of anything yet from Bob's out of all the stuff I've ordered.  Their GF products are top notch and really tasty.  The whole family enjoys this mix.

We are huge fans of Bob's red mills products. Their variety and quality are un-comparable. How ever I had a different experience with this product. We got this product 2 weeks ago and invited few of our friends and family to have an evening party. We made 13 pizzas, (all vegetarian, no meat) and each and every on who ate it got sick(at least 20 of them). The symptoms varied from indigestion, throwing up, breathing trouble etc. Well the party was a disaster and we had to take medications to get the situation under control. I don't know if the problem was with just 1 batch of their product. I reported it to customer service and they issued a full refund.I wish there was way in their site to report the batch numbers so that the product company gets alerted.

This is the best gluten free pizza crust that I have had. My husband said it could be better so I'm not sure if I like it because I can't remember what good pizza crust tastes like or if my husband is just being picky?

When I opened the package I noticed loose flour in the box.  Then I opened the item package and I found that one of the bags of pizza crust mix had burst open leaving its contents in the bottom of the box and covering the other bags of mix.  I found this disappointing because I paid for four bags of pizza mix and I am only able to use three of them.  Otherwise I am satisfied with the product.  I wish there were some way I could replace the damaged bag for a new one.

column9: gloppy, slimey still stuck to utensils
column10: This pizza dough was completely and utterly unusable, without the addition of more than a cup of spelt flour, which defeats the whole GF idea. Luckily we weren't going for GF, just Wheat-free, so I was able to salvage it and the taste was okay; wasn't really pizza dough... but for my son who hasn't had a pizza in two years it was acceptable. I will never use it again!

Granted, I am very new to the gluten free world, but this was hardly palatable.  We are fortunate to have a local pizzeria that sells gluten free take-n-bakes and the difference between the two is amazing.  Too bad Bob's can't get a hold of their recipe! :)

column9: YUCK!  Run like the wind from this stuff
column10: This stuff tastes terrible.  It has a very gross overwhelming dried bean taste to it.  The taste overwhelm everything you put on it....pepperoni, peppers, the sauce, garlic...nothing covers up the taste.  It permeates it and makes the food inedible.

My boyfriend made this pizza (he mixed it by hand, even though it called for a stand mixer). Made a huge pizza that tasted great to me-- very doughy and thick crusted. Very similar tasting to when I would make it from frozen pizzeria dough.My bf said he liked it better than the (gluten filled) pizza he normally ordered and his roommates ate it without realizing that it was gluten free. They loved it and would eat it again. The best pizza I have had since going gluten free.

column9: Can't stand the texture or the taste
column10: I tried this mix by myself, then with my family. Both times I couldn't stand the after taste, even though it smelled really good. It was almost tangy or acrid (unpleasantly sharp). My family was in agreement. I ended up throwing the pizza away. The texture was strange, like it was without substance. I definitely would not go with Bob's Red Mill. I love pizza and wish I could enjoy it with my family. I recently came across a pizza recipe with 63 5-star reviews. I'm definitely going to try that one.

I visited a pizzeria in Queens, NY that uses this mix for their gluten free pizza.  It holds together better than Pamela's pizza crust but the taste of Bob's Red Mill GF pizza crust was absolutely horrid!  Yuck!

I gave this product 3 stars because even though I really disliked it, my kids loved it.  I think that the garbanzo bean flour really overpowered it.  It tasted really bitter and gross to me, and I didn't like the texture.  My kids however, demolished two pizzas over two days.  This is really impressive for my daughter, who doesn't have celiac disease and doesn't even usually eat pizza.  She loved this.

column9: NOT AS GOOD AS I EXPECTED
column10: I'm just trying to eat a bit healthier and eliminating wheat from my diet as much as possible.  I thought I'd give this a try instead of purchasing several ingredients to make my own "special gluten-free" flour.  Very disappointed.  I was expecting pizza crust that would taste ALMOST like the real thing.  Just not worth the hassle of baking 7 - 9 minutes - THEN putting toppings on and baking another 15 - 18 mins.I guess I will just get Digornio Crisply Flatbread Tuscan Chicken pizzas once in a while.  They are much, much lower in carbs and take about 16 - 17 mins to bake AND taste great.I would not buy this again - I have 3 unopened bags that I would sell if I was able to sell a partial box on Amazon.

My children have multiple food allergies, so I am always trying differnt products to find replacements for the normal childhood fun foods. I was disappointed by this dough, It was a wet dough, was just a blob that you sort of pushed around on the pan with no possibilty of making a shape. I did not have trouble with it sticking to the pan. The dough made a thick crust. The texture was not soft or airy, but was crumbly like a biscuit and it had no rise. We are not able to eat eggs, so we replaced it with a flax egg but that just made it look like a whole wheat crust. This is definetly a product we will not but again.

column9: Review of Gluten Free Pizza Crust
column10: The Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Pizza Crust was really bad.  The taste and texture.  Also one of the bags had burst open and there was flour all over in the box.  I ordered three different boxes of Gluten Free products with four bags in each box, and the end bag in each box had burst open.  I just called Bob's Red Mill and they were extremely nice and just sent me the bags right away.
Bad yeasty taste!! It was a gloppy mess, so hard to work with!! I have made "regular" pizza crust dozens of times and this is nothing like it.

column9: received bags opened in sealed box from Red mill and Amazon
column10: This product normally works very well I had several in stock in my cupboard when I open my sealed box found bag opened with pizza crust flour all over the other bags tried to contact Amazon to return or credit unable to get a reply which I find very disturbing....

I hated this crust.  It was so sticky I still can't believe I managed to actually spread it around the pan.  The only thing that made it possible to do so was spraying my hands with crisco every minute to prevent the sticking.  It smelled horrible before it was even baking, smelled terrible while baking, and tasted slightly less horrible than it smelled. It has an overwhelming yeast taste...I would never make this again.

You only know the soul of a company (or a person for that matter) when something goes WRONG. Well there was a mix up on my order. Unfortunately the woman on the phone was unfriendly, accusing and rude! Wow! How can people run a business like this? How can they think it is okay to talk to someone, much less a customer, with such an attitude? Needless to say I did not receive my order in time for my event. It is time to find a different brand of gluten free flours, any ideas?

This is my favorite gluten free pizza mix so far.  I prefer thinner crusts (almost the cracker crisp type crust),  but I'll probably never achieve that with gluten free pizza.  This is the closest thing I've found, however.  I had to experiment a bit to get it right.  This mix makes TWO pizzas, and I use a very large 14" pan  (actually, closer to 16 inches when you include the edges, which curve upwards.)  If you were using a much smaller pizza pan, you might get 3 pizzas out of the mix.I do the mix exactly as per the instructions, let it rise the recommended 30 minutes, THEN I divide the dough into two equal parts.  One part I usually save and refrigerate (in a bowl and topped tightly with either foil or saran wrap) and I've used it up to two or three days later with perfect results.  Then the other half I'll use the day I make it, since I usually only want to do one at a time.  After the dough has risen (it only seems to rise slightly) , I grease the pizza pan  using Crisco...my preference, and I like the results better.  I don't roll it out.  Rather, I put the blob of dough in the center, and use my  hands to punch it down and push it outwards around the pan, bit by bit.  So my hands don't stick to the dough too much, I use a gluten free flour mix such as the Amy's baking mix on my hands as much as needed, so probably a bit of this will get worked in as I spread the dough  out in the pan.  The dough would be impossible to roll out in my opinion, or at least, I don't want to mess with it due to the relative stickiness of the dough.  After the dough is all evenly spread thru the pan and with a bit of an edge, I poke some fork holes around the bottom here and there.  Then I bake the bare crust for about 10 to 12 minutes in the oven at 425...it will be faintly starting to brown at this point.  This pre-cooking is important for gluten free crusts!  Remove from oven, let it cool about 5 minutes, then put on your desired toppings.  With everything on, it goes back into the oven for less than 10 minutes...just to heat everything up and melt the cheese, basically.  The crust will brown a bit more in the process.Even done in such a large pan, the crust isn't as thin as you'd expect, but you avoid the soggy bottom so common to GF crusts.  My whole family loves this pizza and the wheat eaters of the family don't really notice or care about the difference in the crust.  The taste is quite nice, it has that usual yeast flavor of a wheat crust, and there are no weird rice flour tastes at all.  If anything, it's somewhat bland, but that's probably a good thing for a gluten free crust.

This is the best I've tried.  one bag makes me two LARGE rectangular cookie sheet pizzas.  You don't even have to wait for it to rise, it is just as good.  I use my breadmaker to mix it and start the rise usually.  I grease up two LARGE rectangular cookie sheets, the ones with a side that comes up almost an inch high, with olive oil;  I then have a bowl of cold water to keep dipping my hands in, so they don't stick.  pick up half the batch for one pizza with wet hands, add more water, roughly roll into a log, put in pan and take your time pressing down and pushing it to the sides and corners, keep adding water to keep non-stick.  The trick for me is to make it as thin as possible.  Follow directions for pre-cook, and then add ingredients and finish cooking.  Comes out very good.  I've only had better at a restaurant in Worcester MA, Boynton's - awesome.This pizza, I"ll eat 3 or 4 pieces and then freeze the rest.  It heats up fine in the microwave, wrapped in paper towels, 3 or 4 pieces at a time for the next few weeks.  YUM!I use "subscribe and save" with my amazon PRIME account, for free second day shipping, PLUS an additional 15% off.  Can't beat it.  I just set the frequency to 6 months and manually renew it whenever i run out.

This is the best pizza I have made since I started eating gluten free.  This crust actually was crispy & chewy like a pizza instead of crumbly & mushy! I really liked it and will definitely order more.

We not only loved this mix as a pizza crust, but it has become our favorite gf dough for other recipes.  We cut the dough for donuts and fried them, then coated them with powdered sugar or cinnamon- best ever!  And the dough fried and then salted with mustard was the perfect replacement for my mall pretzels.  With garlic and butter, these were the best breadsticks.  I subscribed to 2 cases per month!

This is a good gluten and soy free mix.  I've found most GFSF mixes that people rave about not to be any good without eggs.  This one holds together OK when made with egg replacer or flax seed meal as suggested on the package, but recently I've found it to be even better when I added 1/4 tsp xanthan gum (to the dry mix) on top of that.  To make thin crust, I put the dough on a greased pan (without holes), brush the top with a little oil and cover with a sheet of parchment paper (or plastic wrap), then roll out with a rolling pin.  Carefully and slowly lift the cover sheet and pre-bake the crust according to the instruction, then you can make a pretty good pizza.  I do make my own mix from time to time, but this is the mix I use when my stash runs out and I am short on time.

I'd say this is one of the best gluten free pizza crust mixes out there!  It's simple to make & is not too heavy.  I like to add some italian seasoning to the dry part of the mix before I combine the wet & dry ingredients for some extra flavor.  Even the pizza eaters not on a gluten-free diet like this pizza crust. All in all a good one!  And a decent price too!

Bob's Red Mill  Gluten Free Pizza Crust Mix, 16-Ounce Bags (Pack of 4) works beautifully giving me wheat-free PIZZA. I'd been without pizza pie for so very long and going pizza free was one of the hardest parts of becoming gluten free. Now I make pizza every week!GF foods are never going to act exactly like the wheat varieties, you probably know that by now. When I roll this soft dough on my pizza stone, my hands and roller must be wet with water. A gentle touch is all it needs. I find that using a circular motion as my final move gives me a little 'ditch' to catch any errant sauce.The dough bakes a few minutes without toppings. I find pricking the dough with a fork prevents excess rising. After this first baking, I think one could fill half and fold over for a large calzone, but I've not tried this yet. Normally I top with a Picante sauce, precooked sausage, broccoli, sliced carrots, onions, peppers of several varieties and whatever else is handy. As I'm also casein/dairy sensitive, I use Nutritional Yeast in place of cheese. NY will never be stringy as it's a powder; but it adds a unifying color and extra 'cheezy' taste. The second baking is about 15 minutes. Because my 'cheese' cannot bubble, I use steaming and color of the crust's edge as my done guides.One box of mix makes two crusts. I freeze the uncooked one for the next week. This way a 4-pack lasts me two months and works perfectly for the auto-ship process.Note: If you use raw shrimp on your pizza... drain them very well and pat dry with paper towel. They are delicious even if you don't :-)Love and Light,Pat

Okay, first a few disclaimers...This CAN be a little different to work with, so don't expect the typical, (gorgeous) glutenous, stretchy feel that happens with wheat crusts... (sigh.)It's GONNA be messy... but don't let that stop you. This crust is delicious, and totally worth it.Here's what I do.I follow the directions on the package, with a few substitutions.First, for more flavor punch, I warm some veggie broth in place of the warm water that is called for. I add the yeast right to this, (taking care that it isn't hotter than 105 degrees F, or it will kill the yeast.) I even throw in a smidge of sugar to nudge the yeast along.Then I mix in the dry indredients, which is basically, the mix. To that, I add a bit of flaxseed meal (You may also use flaxseed meal as a substitute for eggs, as it describes on the pkg.- with tasty results. I find that the flaxseed gives the mix a nice texture, so I will often add a bit in addition to eggs when I am not cooking for my vegan friends.)Don't forget the Xantham Gum! This helps out with the texture... helps to give back some of that lovely "glutenous" feel... Amazon has good prices, so snoop around... don't recommend baking without Xantham or Guar gum. Per another reviewer's suggestion, I tried 1/4 tsp. xantham gum for each 16 oz. pkg. I found that advice to be spot on, and I am so glad I decided to try it! Recommended!Then, I add finely chopped, fresh rosemary leaves from the garden... and I do mean, finely... nobody wants chunk of tree in their pizza.This just elevates the crust, almost gives it a focaccia feel. Yummy.Then, after the pan is greased- one review suggested Crisco, and I think I want to try that next- I sprinkle a course grind of kosher or boutique salt-judiciously- on the pan.See, I went to a wonderful gluten free bakery in Washington State- wish I could remember the name of the place, or I would totally give them the credit- did exactly that... finely chopped rosemary, with the lovely crunch of salty goodness on the bottom of the crust as it was baking.Incredible. You MUST try it!!!!!Like others have stated, I do not roll the crust out. I follow the directions on the pkg, which say to use wet hands (mine were more just damp, so that they didn't get sticky) to smooth the crust into the shape I wanted...Then, I poke my fork around to within an inch of the edge... this helps the perimeter to stay puffier then the center, and helps keep the toppings from sliding off the pizza.As others have said, pre- baking is absolutely essential for gluten free crusts. I should try Alton Brown's trick of brushing the edges with a little egg, see if that helps brown up the edges a little more. So many fun things yet to try!Finally, I think that even though this crust is gluten free, and there are definite differences between GF and "regular" baking... I think what Gramma said still holds... "If the dough is too wet, add more flour..." (I always have a stockpile of extra GF flours on hand, just in case... )If I stumble on any other ideas, I will update promptly.This mix is a great addition to my kitchen, it's quick and easy, and tastes great.. (A bunch of us gals went away for a weekend, and I made pizza- first time- using this mix, and everyone was delighted... a double batched scarfed down quicker than I would have thought possible!)Gluten free success!

column9: Good stuff, and not just for pizza
column10: I originally purchased this product to use for making pizza crust.  It makes a decent GF pizza crust, although with some tinkering, I've improved on it.Why I love this and keep buying it, though, is because I use it in nearly all of my baking.  Because I can get it for such a good price through Amazon's subscribe & save program, I've experimented with using it in other baked goods.Mixed 50/50 with BRM brown rice flour, I can use it in place of all-purpose flour in most recipes, and it works like a charm, AND tastes better.:-)  I simply discard the yeast packets.Hope this helps someone!

First, a great thing. Before I had a chance to make a pizza, I tried some of this flour to make banana oatmeal cookies. They came out great, just like Mom used to make. I'm so grateful I found that I can use this stuff to do that.As far as making a pizza. I added a little salt and basil to the mix for flavor, made a pizza, and it was pretty darn good. It's really hard to get the "dough" to spread out, I used a wetted rubber spatula and a lot of patience, but got the pan covered. With a homemade sauce, and some cheeses and mushrooms, it was SO good to have a pizza again. Perfect? maybe not, but very enjoyable. I'll do it again. I guess that's the question, isn't it? Would you bother to do it again? So, recommended, try it and see if you can deal with it.

column9: A Chewy NY Style Foldable Crust!
column10: I really thought good NY style pizza was a thing of my pre gluten free past...like Life cereal and licorice. This pizza crust changed that. The first attempt, near perfect. The second, some changes were made. I let the dough rise overnight in the 'fridge. This gave it an even more elastic texture. I used probably 2-3 tablespoons of water to spread the crust out evenly in the pan but due to par baking...this works well. Don't be afraid to use the water or you may have an unspreadable glob, and not a pizza crust. The resulting pizza is amazing. You can fold the slice without any crumbling, even 2-3 day old leftovers retain their "real" pizza qualities. The topped crust has all the texture and chew I've come to expect in pizza. The un-topped "lip" of crust that forms the pizza has a slight "beany" taste from the bean flour in the mix. I solved that by making a rectangular, southern CT style pizza...totally topped, no crust lip. I will also try adding seasoning and garlic to a crust sometime and see what that does. I'd rather pizza, than no pizza...and this is the best GF pizza mix I have tried to date.

column9: Great for pizza crust or a flat bread
column10: I found this mix to be great for a pizza crust, or a crispy flat bread. The first (we use up to 11 minutes) and second baking times (8 to 12 minutes depending on the number of toppings)in a 425 degree oven will vary with your oven and your preferences.  I also found that you can actually make up to four pizza crusts out of one bag that are about nine inches in diameter. This of course depends on the number of servings that you need at one time, how thick you like the crust (we like a thin crust) and the appetites. The pre-made dough keeps very well in the refrigerator for up to 5 days and if you let the refrigerated dough rest for 30 minutes before the first baking as the directions state, you will get a very nice crispy crust with a soft bread-like center. The pre-baking process allows you to load the pizza up with your favorite toppings (up to five toppings with double cheese and the crust does not get soggy!)and get a nice melt on the cheese with the second baking.  It makes a very tasty flat bread (cover with cheese and your favorite vegetables for the second baking)to serve with soups and heartier stews.  I've tried many different types of pizza crusts including the prepared frozen ones, other mixes and this is the best so far.  If you keep some ready made dough in the refrigerator it makes a great substitute for bread in a pinch!
love this mix. It tastes great and is easy to use. My family has Celiac Disease and can't have gluten so it is fantstic for us.

Fantastic!  How to do it: I used the mix + oil and 1 egg + 1 TBSP flaxseed meal (combined w/3Tbsp H2o)...I mixed by hand w wooden spoon until just incorporated (like muffins), added garlic powder along w yeast mixture. Divided into 1/2s, let rise in bowl atop oven as it preheated. Used 1/2 dough on 12" cheap aluminum plate, greased w olive oil. After 8-9 min, removed from oven, flipped pizza over w BIG spatula, then added toppings. Cook another 10-15, then perfect! Even BF loved it,

The "dough" part is a bit misleading...this is the wettest dough I've ever worked with, even way more so than scone dough.  It's near impossible to work with. If you're hoping for a super thin crust, you won't be able to attain that with this. First of all, it does not really rise, leaving you with wet slop to push apart on the pan. Don't try it on a pizza pan with holes, either. If you keep your hands soaking wet, you may be able to spread it out some but not as thin as I would really like. Once baked, it's a very uneven crust due to the difficulty of spreading it. It also has a bit of a "funky" taste but my husband likes it a lot. It's the only gluten-free pizza crust I've tried thus far, so I have nothing to compare it with.

I have been a huge fan of this pizza crust mix since my son was found to be NCGI almost a year ago. However, the last two shipments of this product have had opened packages and flour spilling inside the box. The first one was a minor opening, but the one I just received had over 1/3 of the top seal undone, and a good 1/3 cup of flour was spilled all inside the box. Something needs to be done about quality control of the bag sealing, because improperly sealed bags were what caused both leaks.The dough tastes great, though, and it's easy to work with!!

column9: Yummy. If it's gross, you're doing it wrong...
column10: I have tried several recipes for gluten-free pizza dough, and it's a lot of work. We started using this because it's so much easier than mixing it yourself. I really like this dough. I have read the other reviews and have no idea what they're talking about--this is good stuff. The only reason I give it 4 stars instead of 5 is because the bottom doesn't get quite crispy enough, while they edges do. The flavor is good, though!

column9: Prepare for slime & get your hands wet! My pizza fanatic family love it:)
column10: We have been on the search for a good gluten free pizza crust for about a year and the first time we tried BRM I did not like it at all.  It was just a slimy mess and I couldn't get it to 'roll' out in the pan.  We were out of the expensive precooked GF crusts and I found a bag of this in the back of the freezer....it was pizza night and we were desperate.  This time I made sure I followed the directions completely and allowed the dough to rise the full time.  I greased my 2 large pizza pans with olive oil.  Having read tips for spreading pizza dough that suggested having very wet hands, I thought I might as well try it.  SLiMy dough and wet hands this is going to be disguisting!  Once I got over the sliminess I found the dough spreads very well by just pressing it out with your wet hands.  Your hands need to be almost dripping wet.  I run my hands under water and lightly tap off some of the water so I don't drip all over.  The dough slides very well!  Once you get the hang of it, spreading the dough is easy.  The good news is my pizza fanatic family loves it.  I've even had gluten eating friends come over for pizza night and they enjoyed it as well.  It works well for leftovers in school lunches too.
This product is nice, I am an Indian & My daughter has celiac, & this product is a survivor.  Besides making pizza we even use it for making chapatis, roti, & Naan.

column9: Really, really good - ignore the negative reviews!
column10: I hadn't purchased this on Amazon due to the fair number of negative reviews...a big mistake on my part!I generally prefer to blend all of my own flours, but with four young kids, 'life happens' and I need to be more realistic about taking shortcuts where I can find them. We've just moved into a new house, and I wanted to make homemade pizza - but of course all of my gear (including flours) isn't unpacked yet. In a pinch, I picked up a single bag of this at Target to give it a try.It was super! It *is* essential to spread the dough with wet hands...and no, it doesn't handle like regular dough during this process. Then again, what GF dough does? I used egg whites in the recipe, not full eggs due to cholesterol issues and there were no negative consequences.After baking the dough to a nice light golden color, we brushed a light layer of extra-virgin olive oil on it. This was followed by a very light sprinkling of sea salt. We then covered the crust with fresh basil (we happened to have this from our own container garden) and then thin slices/pieces of mozzarella. Tomatoes were eliminated as this mum is on a strict no-sugar diet, but it wasn't missed by anyone -- this was truly delicious!In fact, it was such a hit that we repeated the pizzas a few days later for a family movie night. This time, I purchased two bags of the mix locally - this quantity can easily make three large rectangular pizzas (using standard cookie/jelly roll pans). This amount was plenty for a large family and will be repeated when we have guests over. I should add that I was able to simple double the batch with no negative consequences...sometimes GF recipes are fussy and I'm unable to double- or triple- batches, which is a bummer as it takes much longer.Needless to say, I added this to my subscribe & save orders this morning. It's a great bargain and according to the kids it's 'waaaaayyyyyy better than pizza from Italian restaurants' - and a whole lot healthier, without sacrificing our GF nutritional goals!The next time we make this, I'll upload some pictures. It is so good - and so healthy!

This product was very easy to prepare.  One warning to those unfamiliar with GF 'dough'...it's more like a very thick muffin batter.While wheat flour has that stretchiness, this does not, simply because it's gluten-free.  I think if I had been more prepared for the consistency, it wouldn't have seemed so odd.That said, it was easy to mix (I did it by hand) and it did rise a bit during the waiting period.I added dried oregano and chopped fresh garlic to mine, and will add more seasonings next time I make it.Spreading the "batter" is not hard, if you are prepared.  I used a cookie sheet and made one rectangular pizza from one package.  Make sure you oil/spray the pan and you will need to spread the mixture using wet hands.  Again, since this is not wheat, you will be doing more spreading and patting down than stretching.You bake the crust first and then add toppings. I used jarred spag sauce, sliced mushrooms, sliced onions and shredded mozz cheese.  Baked it for about 18 minutes and it was perfect.This will not fool anyone into thinking this is a traditional wheat pizza dough.  There is no comparison, as wheat has totally different characteristics than these ingredients.  BUT, this product is great.  Really, it does not have much of any taste at all, and you can add whatever herbs and spices you want to the mixture to customize it.  The texture was slightly crunchy and even my husband loved it.Since this is my first GF mix, I have no other point of reference, so I can't give it 5 stars.  BUT, I will continue to use this product on a regular basis and I'm looking forward to trying the all-purpose flour I ordered at the same time.

My 13 year old daughter has to eat gluten free and this pizza dough is great.  I make a 9 X 13 sheet and bake without toppings.  I slice it up individually and freeze separately for later.  When she wants pizza I just pull one out, defrost in microwave, add toppings and bake.  I added a sprinkle of garlic powder before the toppings as she likes the extra garlic.

I have tried several gluten free pizza crust recipes with mixed results.  This mix is GREAT!  I've fed it to the rest of my family several times (none of them are gluten free) and they LOVE it!  I highly recommend it!  I also am dairy/casein free and this crust works out just fine.  Is great w/some soy cheese on top!

This is an easy mix that takes only minutes.  I don't use the yeast, since it's not necessary and takes too much time for my chaotic schedule, but the flavor is a hit with my kids-- both for the pizza crust and in other meals.Amazon's subscription service is amazingly convenient!

column9: best thin crust gluten free pizza!!
column10: 1. It's gluten free, which means it will not be exactly like a "real" pizza dough2. It says to use wet hands to spread, but I get the best  results by using a big wet spatula. This way, you can really spread it out to get a nice thin crust.3. My kids love this pizza, which is amazing,since they balk at a lot of gf things.4. You must prebake before adding toppings! Don't skip this step!5. Like most gf,it doesn't work well as  leftovers. Eat while fresh and hot..not as great the next day!6. I always add a touch of olive oil brushed on the crust.. Gives it a touch of fat that makes it just a bit better!

Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Pizza Crust mix is one of the best purchases I have made of Bob's products. My husband misses pizza and I have made homemade pizza crusts for him. The amount of ingredients needed to make a homemade gluten-free pizza crust is unbelievable. It is also very time consuming to gather all the ingredients. I love the convenience of simply opening a bag of Bob's pizza crust mix and preparing it in my mixer. No muss, no fuss! The taste is great. This bag makes 2 pizzas and they reheat for lunches very well. I will always make sure I have this item in my pantry. I would recommend Bob's Red Mill products to anyone that needs gluten-free products.

column4: K. Goyette "A voracious reader and experiment...
column10: This is excellent, convenient, looks like and cooks up like the real thing. All the teenagers in my house love it. The WFGF dough can be hard to work with sometimes but just use water on your hands and smooth the dough onto the pizza pan and you're good to go. We like to bake the crust for about 8 minutes before we put the sauce and toppings on. Delicious and now we can have pizza again! YAY!
yeap would buy this again - after going wheat free I have missed pizza so much, but now; I can have it again.

column9: I'm not GF and I love this!
column10: I don't have any sort of gluten allergy or intolerance but was looking into GF products just because less gluten seems healthy. Baking has never been my forte so it was a bit scary delving into GF baking, which I know even less about, but this was basically effortless!I bought a single bag of this at Whole Foods to try and I absolutely loved it and ordered a case on Amazon a few days later. I made two decent sized pizzas with the first bag and froze the second one (after baking the crust and putting on the toppings but before actually baking the toppings) and they both turned out amazingly. The dough is softer, stays together well, and the crust is lovely and crunchy. I'm a huge fan.I do prefer letting the dough rise for 30min instead of 20, but it doesn't make a huge difference. Also make sure you spread the dough with wet hands! I usually have to wet them several times while spreading it. And make sure the baking pan is well greased!

column9: Bob's Red Mill Pizza Crust Mix
column10: Best stuff EVER!  Rolls out just like the real stuff...  I use a little corn starch to roll it out and then put some corn meal in the bottom of the pan to give it extra crunch.  I also bake it without the toppings for about eight minutes.

Before making this crust the first time, I read as many of the reviews as possible which was extremely helpful.  Now that I've made it a few times I have started to make some of my own discoveries.  I make the dough exactly the way it tells you to on the package, but I don't divide it before letting it rest for 30 mins.  Also, I don't roll out the dough.  I pretty much just spread it around with the back of a spoon or with my fingertips (keep a bowl of water next to you to dip your fingertips in so the dough doesn't stick to you).  Keep spreading the dough out thinner and thinner to desired thickness.  It does puff up a bit when baked, so the thinner the better.  I have found that you can even stretch the dough so thin that there are holes left in the dough, but once you add toppings no one will ever know.  When cooking the dough, put it in longer than you think you should.  I wait until all the edges are brown, and the middle is starting to color.  My husband was bummed when we first started eating gluten free pizzas (he's not gluten intollerant, just me) because he said they were gummy and gross and had a weird after-taste.  Now that we have this mix, and now that I make the crust super super super thin and crispy, he says he can't even tell a difference.  This mix has definitely been a God-send.

column9: A good substitute for wheat pizza crust!
column10: This is a very good value for a gluten-free pizza dough mix.  One package should make two medium-sized pizzas. I only used half of the pizza dough (I put the rest in the refrigerator) and I ended up with a good-sized round pizza that works perfectly for planning on 8 slices of pizza. I used a mixture of water, ground flaxseed and chia seeds (already gelled) as an egg substitute and it worked fine (actually I think that it improves the pizza crust in that it adds healthy fat and fiber).  Just after I started to  add grated cheese, sauce, spinach and onions, I realized that I was supposed to bake the dough without toppings first.  I turned the oven down to 350 degrees, then I baked the entire pizza with toppings for 25 minutes.  I then turned the oven up to 450 degrees, put the pizza on a lower rack and baked for a little while longer.  It came out crispy and tasty.Backing up the process a little - the dough was easy to work with even though it did separate some.  I didn't use an electric mixer.  I just kneaded the dough with my hands, then let it rise for 20 minutes.  I took a Crisco-greased flat baking sheet sprinkled with cornmeal and then created a pizza pie circle of dough with a slightly elevated border of dough with wet fingers.  I also put olive oil all around where the crust was exposed.The overall result was a very tasty and satisfying pizza pie.  It should be noted that this is not low-carb at all, but there is a good amount of fiber in each serving.  One serving is 1/8 of the package or 57g and each serving contains 45g of carbohydrate and 4g of dietary fiber.  The mix contains brown rice, potato starch and flour, millet, sorghum, tapioca, evaporated cane juice, xanthan gum, yeast (separate package), sea salt, guar gum.  There are 200 calories per serving in the dry mix with only 10 calories from fat.There are no soy products or tree nuts in the mix, but the facility manufactures products with these ingredients.Update:I used this pizza crust mix to make a very substantial and delicious gluten free artisan-style bread.  I followed the recipe for the cinnamon buns on the package, but added milk instead of water and only 1 tablespoon of sugar.  I also added whole chia seeds.  The end result was impressive - a gorgeous loaf of bread that would be a great addition to any occasion.  The only thing that I noticed is that the first day that I tried it out, it really sort of swelled in my stomach and created a very almost uncomfortable full feeling - and that was after eating a small amount.Update:  After using this pizza crust mix to create two excellent pizzas, I can highly recommend this product.I stored the other half of the pre-made dough in the refrigerator for several days.  Last night I used a flat baking sheet with a thin layer of olive oil sprinkled in the middle with coarsely ground corn meal (polenta).  I moistened my fingers with water and spread the dough easily into a large circle and then sprinkled olive oil and seasonings on the dough and pre-baked it.  I then added various cheeses and rinsed canned crabmeat, fresh basil and herbs and seasonings.  The result was a very impressive tasting and looking "white" pizza.  This pizza crust mix wins on all counts - taste, ease of use and price.  It costs about $1.25 per medium/large pizza crust with Subscribe & Save.

column9: Quick & Tasty Gluten Free Pizza Crust Alternative
column10: Easy, quick, and tastes great.  It's not the same as wheat pizza dough, so don't expect the same flavor or consistency.  I prefer the eggless version (use ground flax & water as egg substitute).  Sticks to hands when spreading on pizza pan, but a little water or oil solves the problem.  Subscribe & Save at Amazon is a great price.

I love pizza.  Since my doctor told me that I need to be gluten free, I have been very sad without my favorite meal of pizza and beer.  I was excited when I found this product.  The first time I made it, the texture threw me off a little, but it was OK.  I had major digestion issues for the 12 hours after consuming.  I gave it another chance a few weeks later.  Still just OK.  Edible, but not that good, with major stomach pain after.  I still have two bags of this in my pantry waiting to be used.

I've been gluten free for the past eight months (self diagnosed Celiac). This is by far the best pre-made pizza crust flour available -- delicious and reasonably priced. (But seriously, what else would you expect for Bob's Redmill?!) The recipe is foolproof, flavor has no aftertaste, and the texture is fluffy. I've gone 'outside the box' and went so far as to make cheesy bread and biscuits with the dough as well. Great product.

My girlfriend and i live a Vegan lifestyle, teetering on plant-based, and the combination of the two means we dont consume oil or eggs, two standards of baking, and ingredients specifically called for here. They suggest replacing eggs with flaxseed meal, which we do, and we use Emergen-C Egg Replacer as well. After some experimentation, we found we were able to make a great pizza dough that suited our diets perfectly using these packages. The other plus here is that the blend actually tastes good as well. We eat pizza at least once a week on average, and this Bob's Red Mill mix is the one we always use. In fact, with a little practice and toying with added ratios, our pizzas have reached the mouthwatering stage. So, i consider this to be a great product with an equally great value. Btw, if anybody wants the specific mix recipe we are currently using, feel free to email me by clicking on my profile and i will send you a copy. It is very simple (of course, owning a pizza stone is fairly essential as well).Enjoy!
I wish this tasted good.  I can't describe the taste but it was the worst out of all of the gluten free crusts we have tried. A big disappointment.

Thank heaven for this product. I missed pizza so much, and I was afraid that the mix would be unrealistic or disgusting. This pizza crust mix is very tasty, has a really good texture, and it produced a satisfying pie. Highly recommended for the folks out there who are heartbroken over the loss of gluten foods, because this will give you back one of the things you love.

column9: I really like this product...easy to prepare good for veggie pizza:-)
column10: I really liked this ...I wanted to have pizza...but I wanted it to be a little more healthy than the regular pizza bread...yum, yum good...

I had never made my own pizza before. I made a large 16" pie the other day with this. Followed the directions to the letter and it came out wonderfully! The crust is chewy yet crispy. The pizza was on par with my favorite local pizza place (Jockamo's in Indy) and was superior to any frozen pizza i've ever had from DiGiorno or Freschetta. I was pleasantly surprised with how well it came out. And now i can eat pizza at home again since going gluten-free 8 months ago.

column9: wonderful for multiple allergy pizza fans!
column10: My son has many food allergies. On-top of his allergies, he is a very picky eater. We had tried several other kinds of GF pizza crust mixed with no luck. This was the best crust we have tried!  We use flax seed and water instead of egg. Also i mixed it with a fork just until it looked mixed together. I let the dough rise 20 minutes. I split it in half and refrigerated half wrapped tightly in saran wrap. (lasts up to three days.)  And using lots of water on my hands the whole time, made the rest into two small 6 in pizza forms.baked ten minutesadded toppingsbake 5 minutes.Crispy on the outside and soft and airy/doughy on the inside! the closest thing to real pizza we've found! We are a customer for life now!:)my super picky 2 year old LOVED it!THANKS FOR THE AWESOME PRODUCT! DON'T EVER CHANGE A THING!!! :)

I'm comfortable making homemade pizza crust from wheat flour so I just did the same things I always have with great success. I used half the bag for one crust and it was LARGE. I used the whole yeast pack even for half the mix. I have other yeast for next time. Mix the wet and dry ,the dough should not be wet or you can't roll it out good. Instead of rising the dough in the bowl, I greased my hands with olive oil (don't use water) put the dough on a cold, oiled pizza stone, flipped the dough ball over, rolled thin with an oiled rolling pin, made an edge around then let it rest for about 15 min. I sprinkled garlic powder, oregano and basil all over the raw dough. I baked for 10 min, let it cool a little then topped (dont over sauce,it'll be soggy) and finished cooking until very crisp. It was very good but even better after reheating the next day...even more crisp. I thought it was going to over cook  but its better that way. I would buy this again. Its the first gluten free pizza I have ever had. The taste is just as good as a wheat crust! I was very happy with the pizza as were my husband and child.
We love this pizza crust mix.  We make pizza weekly with it.  It is not too crisp and not too doughy.  We make it vegan, using ener g egg replacer.  It comes out great every time!

I've made many gluten pizza crust recipes from scratch, using multiple (expensive) flours and all sorts of recipes. In general, they don't rise well and taste very much like cardboard. Bob's actually rises and has the texture of a foccacia flat bread.  It is NOT the wettest GF pizza crust mix I've run across ... several of the scratch ones are absolutely like batter. This is more like a loose dough. Also, I mixed it using the dough hook on my KitchenAid mixer and I'm told that may have made a big difference in the dough consistency. I followed the recipe exactly, letting it rise in a warm (garage) for 20 minutes.  It is sticky, but I followed the directions and kept wetting my hands to pat it into a round shape--be patient, wet your palms as soon as it starts to stick and go around the shape 3 or 4 times -- it will work.  You can also grease your hands with olive oil if you prefer that method.  I also did NOT use a pizza pan, but instead patted it into a round on a heavy duty lipped cookie sheet and it was perfect.  As it makes 2 crusts, I mixed a bit of dried basil and powdered garlic into the dough of one crust and that made it even better. I also patted the 2nd one quite a bit thinner, as the first time I thought it was about right, but once it rose, it was quite thick. This will be our 'go to' mix from now on.

I've been gluten free for a few years now and realize that getting decent gluten free products is not that easy. Baking them yourself seems to be the logical options, but cost and ability are great hindrances for many. I enjoy making pizza crust from scratch as I know exactly what is in it and in what quantities, and I can fudge the recipe to make a crispier or doughier pizza, depending on what I want. However, when one flour or another is out, or my starch is gone, or I'm visiting a friend or family member's house, I grab this pizza crust mix.It mixes well every time without fail and tastes acceptable. Just as the other reviewers say, the crust isn't dry or crumbly, it holds together well, and makes a fair amount of pizza. It's nothing to write mom about, but it is decent, consistent pizza dough.

I bought this pizza dough from a local grocery store and it tasted so much like "normal" crust that I bought a box online.  My boyfriend is recently diagnosed gluten free and I want to cook for him.  I am a lunchlady at a private school.  I also have students and staff who are gluten challenged.  It is easy to mix and a breeze to cook.  I would recommend it

I haven't found a better GF mix. This is wonderful. I grew up in an Italian American family and married an Italian American too, this is the best crust we've ever tasted, GF or not. In our home we add a little sugar and honey to the mix and knead it for about 5-10 minutes which gives the dough a lovely flavor and texture. This dough also makes great soft pretzels which get gobbled right up in our home! For the money, you can't beat it. We're able to get 8 crusts out of a case and with subscribe and save its an incredible value and it works for us because we go through it so fast!

column9: Best gluten free pizza crust I have found by far!
column10: This stuff is easy to make and is a great substitute for the real thing.  I have used it about a dozen times and really like the taste and texture.  Friends have eaten it and liked it.  They noticed it was different than normal pizza crust but liked it just the same.

I really do like this pizza crust mix.  I use it for more than pizza crust, I also use it to make biscuits, thicken gravy, coat chicken etc. and it always comes through with flying colors.  I would not hesitate to recommend this product to anyone needing to keep gluten out of their diet.  Yes, you can make your own mixes and I often do, especially for bread, but it is messy and I do not always want to have to do that.  This is a great "go-to" packaged mix from the great folks at Bob's Red Mill and here at Amazon.

We've tried many gluten free pizza crust mixes. This is by far the best. When I first made it, however, I began to think this would not turn out! I was unable to roll the dough. It was kind of sticky. Keep your hands slight wet and just "work it out" on the pizza pan. Spread it out evenly, re-wetting hands when needed. It takes time but I promise you, it will be fine!!! I have the pizza pan with holes in it, and the crust turns out heavenly crisp, which we like!! The prices here on Amazon are terrific too! Fast shipping! We will continue to buy many of our gluten free staple items from Amazon!! Thank you Amazon! You guys rock!

column9: love it!!  Except for yeast "rise" (it doesn't??)
column10: First off: I assure you that "I know pizza."  I'm an ex-New Yorker, and I've basically lived off of pizza my entire life.  I made pizza at home for years before I was recently diagnosed with celiac.  So I know what good pizza "should" taste like.I've tried the Glutino mix and a couple other mixes for pizza, and the Bob's Red Mill mix is by far the best I've tried so far.  It's easy to make, can be spread out with your hands (without using utensils), feels relatively close to regular dough, has a very good texture, and an excellent taste--almost like a gourmet pizza crust (warning: you may find the taste slightly different from what you're used to at first, since most people probably haven't tried a pizza that tastes like this; but I got used to it right away and liked it very much).It can be a tiny bit limp, and it's got a relatively narrow baking "window" in which to get the texture right--too undercooked and it'll be too limp and soggy, too overcooked and the browned parts of the pizza will taste kind of bitter and weird.  But I've managed to find a sweet spot, and it's fantastic.  I use the flaxseed option (no eggs), and bake for about 11 minutes on lowest rack at 450, then sauce and cheese, then back into oven at 450 for another 8 minutes.  Works great.  I HIGHLY recommend using the flaxseed option in place of the normal eggs method.The one thing that bugs me--I can't seem to get the dough to rise hardly at all.  It works fine anyway; but for some reason the yeast just does not seem to make the dough any bigger.  I've done the "let rest for 20 minutes" thing after mixing, and yet I can't get any action out of the yeast.  Would love to hear if others have had more luck in this regard?Anyway, if you're looking for a very good GF mix for pizza, look no further, this is great.  Obviously, everyone's tastes will be different--some people may try this and hate the taste or texture.  But I'd venture to say that this will be a winner for most people.  If I could've rated this 4 and a half stars, I would've--it's not absolutely perfection (5 stars), but it's better than just "very good" (4 stars).
I really did not like the baked texture of this product.  I discarded half of the pizza.

I love this pizza mix. After going gluten free i was very upset about not being able to have my deep dish pizza but with this mix i can have it and it tastes great. I add about a cup 1/3 to 1/2 of cooked grated potato and it makes an excelent deep dish pizza that even my picky boyfriend loves!!

After reading the reviews I ordered a case and boy was I  disappointed.We tried both the thick and thin and both were equally as bad.We love pizza and this just does not cut it at allI make my from scratch with Jules' Flour or Better Batter Flour and when in a time crunch have used Chebe frozen dough or Schar's rounds. If I have to make it from scratch I will go back  to using Jules' or Better Batter or even 'Cause Your Special mix..the rest of this case is being donated to a food bank.
Taste pretty good.  I am a regular user of Bob's Red Mill.  However, I like Namaste brand pizza better.

column9: If your'e gluten challenged this is the one!
column10: This product is absolutely worth purchasing if you are a gluten challenged person. Of course it's not a wheat pizza crust, but even still it's very good. It's got a nice chewy texture and making it is a snap ( I only use 1 egg). I can actually get three 12 inch shells out of the package very easily. I divide the dough into three balls and don't let it rise. I freeze two of them for later use which seems to work just fine. When I spread the dough into a shell on a baking pan, I then let it rise in the oven for a bit at low temp. Then I precook the shell so it is just starting to brown on the edges. Put the toppings on and finish cooking. For us gluten challenged folks, this is the real deal.

column9: A tasty GF pizza crust mix
column10: I thought this mix made a Gluten Free pizza crust that was very acceptable. There is nothing like a well made gluten filled pizza crust but when that isn't possible this is very tasty and doesn't have too many additives.

column9: I rarely complain but this tastes like Doggy Biscuits, so if you like them...
column10: I hate giving negative reviews and sometimes people are just Fuss-buckets but I am not--so read this review knowing that I'm not big on complaining. I cook and bake A LOT. I do a lot of my own Gluten Free Recipes so I'm no novice.  I've used a Ready Made Gluten Free crust (EnerG Foods Rice Pizza Shells) here from Amazon that I pre-cooked and it's not too bad as long as you pre-cook with Olive Oil before you add the toppings and then again, after. I wanted even better--so we ordered these Bob's Red Mill Pizza Crust bags. I have made this 2x now. The first time I followed directions to the T and it turned out rubbery and gooey. The 2nd time I read EVERY review and followed the extra instructions. My Husband and I are sitting here with full bellies from this pizza--because we ate the yummy TOPPINGS, only. On an EFFORT note: It doesn't take that long--cause you let the dough rise -while you are making the chicken and onions and garlic & peppers, etc for the pizza. I even pre-seasoned the dough & forked it & oiled it and cooked it and made sure it was VERY flat. After 15 mins, I grabbed a bite of the crispy dough-before I added the toppings and it tasted like...DOG FOOD biscuits! (Now, on a side note--how could I know--you ask--well, doesn't EVERY kid taste their doggies food and you don't forget that taste) Anyway, Toppings were yummy---and I don't mind a little more effort on the crust if it taste SUPERB--but DOG FOOD PIZZA CRUST is NOT what I would recommend to ANYONE. On that note--we did feed the rest of the crust to our doggies. Bottom line--we are going back to those pre-made crusts.  The rest of the bags?  Garbage!
My family and I love the crust made with this mix.  I do add some Italian seasoning to it just for more flavor.

This flour is awesome, we used to buy lot of pizzas from pizza shops which are unhealthy high in fats, since we tried this flour we are making healthy and delicious pizzas at home itself.Thanks to Amazon for selling this amazing product.

A great pizza mix, especially if you love your pizza base thin and crispy, as I have always got the best results from making it that way. You would never know it is gluten free when you taste the end result.

column9: For all you gluten-free junkies that need pizza...
column10: This stuff is great when your pizza craving is so irrefutable that you almost give in to your celiac problem.Not quite the pizza dough your used to but still good enough and easy enough to make and keep yourself gluten free. Be sure to get yourself some pizza pans, pizza sauce (make your own with fresh ingredients) and some toppings and you won't be disappointed.  You will need some olive oil and eggs to make the pizza dough. Thanks Bob and cool hat!

column9: Very sticky and slimy, but good flavor
column10: I made this dough on a dry day, with the air conditioner running, and used less water than called for.  I ended up with a VERY sticky, slimy dough.  So sticky I couldn't press this dough out because it stuck horribly to my hands and wouldn't stay together.  After reading other reviews, it seems there may be some tricks for dealing with this.That said, the flavor was pretty good, and it did puff up in the oven more than I expected it to.  Overall, I'll probably stick to making my own dough, but I would use this in a pinch.If you don't want to make your own GF dough, this will work, but know you're going to get sticky.

We made pizza the night it came, I will admit the crust tastes different and has a little different texture, but it is good it will take my daughter a little while to get used to it (she is 4) she ate some but was not an instant fan.  That is okay I am going to try the cinnamon rolls on the package we will see about those.

I've used several different GF pizza mixes, and this is my favorite!  It's not sticky dough like some I have tried, its really easy to work with, and comes out nice and soft, and not hard as a rock! I would highly recommend it to anyone!  I now keep it stocked on my shelves!

Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Pizza Crust is really easy to make and it tastes great!I tried different mixes, but this one is by far the best I have come across. It doesn't have that crumbly texture and horrible bean taste that some of the other gluten free mixes have. This mix tastes just like a real, "bready" pizza crust. I haven't had pizza for a long time, and already thought I'll have to give it up forever until I tried this crust. Wow, I will probably make pizza more often again...Oh yes, make sure to wet your hands while working with the dough, or it will stick to your fingers like crazy (smile).

I tried some different dough-handling techniques, to see if I could improve upon the package instructions, since it came out kind of biscuit-y:Instead of using wet hands to shape the dough, I sprinkled it with some white rice flour, and rolled it out between 2 rice-floured pieces of wax paper. Then I peeled off the top paper, flipped the rolled-out dough onto the pizza stone, peeled off the other piece of wax paper, then shaped the rough edges by hand. Baked it according  the instructions (7 minutes at 425), then brushed the entire crust with olive oil (helps keep the crust more soft and pliable), added the toppings and put it back in the oven to finish baking.The flavor and texture are as close to "real" pizza as gluten-free gets. The flavor is neutral, but if you find it too bland, just sprinkle the dough with some salt or garlic powder after you roll it out. I've tried quite a few other brands, and also tried my hand at making GF pizza dough from scratch, but this is the best I have tried; I don't even miss wheat flour crust anymore :)The price is economical, too; I usually divide the dough into 4 portions (to make 4 individual 10-inch crusts)and freeze them after the initial 7 minute baking. You can also make a large Sicilian pizza by rolling the dough out on a rimmed cookie sheet.

column9: The kids asked me to order more!
column10: My kids and I have celiac and in addition, the kids are allergic to eggs.  The babysitter made this for them using Ener-G Egg Replacer instead of eggs or the suggested substitute, ground flaxmeal.  The kids loved it, even better than my homemade GF pizza crust I've been making for years.  I didn't get to try it warm out of the oven, but at room temperature, later.  It was a bit rubbery and tasted more like a biscuit-textured crust than a typical wheat based crust, but with toppings it made for a decent pizza.  I don't think you can even compare it to one made with wheat even though it's been about seven years since I've had one.  The kids couldn't stop raving about it though, so I'll be ordering more.

This mix is fantastic.  Most other pizza crust mixes take a lot longer to make and rise.  The rise time for this is only 20 minutes.  It also makes for great breadsticks!  My only suggestion is not to sign up for the subscription to get it because the price varies so widely from $11 to $15 and you may not be getting the deal you had hoped for.

column9: Sorry, I wanted this to be great, but it isn't
column10: Since going gluten free, I've been hoping to find a good GF pizza crust. I have a lot of respect for the Bob's Red Mill brand, and I sincerely hoped they had pulled off the perfect gluten free pizza crust.They failed.  But, I don't blame them.  I think if anyone could pull it off, they could.  I appreciate thay they're trying.  I may just have to accept that a perfect gluten free substitute just does not exist.

This is very good. You can't even tell it's gluten free. I love thin crust anyway and this makes a nice thin and crispy crust. It's also easier to make than regular gluten containing mixes because it's not so doughy and you don't have to knead it. There is a trick to spreading it in the pan - you have to make sure your hands are very wet - and don't forget to prebake it before topping.

this ia an absolutely fantastic product!  wonderful taste and texture with just enough "chew" to make every bite a delight.  I have celiac disease and have to search out good products to eat through trial and error.  I HAVE FOUND MY PIZZA DOUGH!

column9: Best one I have found so far...
column10: I have tried a few other brands but this one tastes the most like regular pizza crust. The only thing I think it could use is some salt for flavor, as it is rather bland, so I will add maybe 1/2 tsp or more of salt the next time. Could even add some oregano or garlic powder to the dough mix to give it more flavor.

This gluten free pizza crust mix is a great start but it needs a boost of flavor. In addition to adding extra olive oil, I add garlic powder, parmesan cheese and basil to the dry mix before adding it to the water and yeast mixture. I've made it into rolls and flat bread as well as pizza crust. It's very important to wet your hands as directed when patting the dough into the pan. I use one package of pizza crust for two 11X17 inch pans. I would recommend this product to others who have to watch their gluten consumption.

This pizza crust was great!! My 2.5 year old son has had severe food allergies (to milk, eggs, wheat, and all mammal meats) his whole life, so he has never had pizza before. We made this pizza crust tonight (omitting the eggs and using the flaxmeal recommended on the package), with pizza sauce, Daiya mozzarella cheeze, and chicken sausage and not only did he LOVE it, but so did my husband and I, who have no food allergies and know what it *should* taste like! I just used a regular sized cookie sheet which I greased with spray olive oil, then kept a small bowl of warm water near by to dunk my hands in while I smooshed the dough into an even layer.This was so easy, very tasty, and will now be a regular in our meal rotation!

column9: Some of the Best Pizza Dough Ever!
column10: I like making pizza at home for several reasons, one of the main reasons being i think its better for you than some of the greasy slices you can buy and for another homemade pizza tends to taste better as well... I've always had a difficult time finding a good pizza dough recipe though, and lets face it, if the dough tastes gross, its kinda downhill from there :P at least for me it is. A friend of mine recommended this dough, she can't eat things with gluten in it. I asked her if the taste of the dough was affected by it being gluten free? she assured me it was amazing and I would not taste a difference. She was right, not only is this dough gluten free, it tastes AMAZING!! It was easy to make as well, just needed water, eggs and oil. The directions were easy to understand and follow also. Each 16oz bag i found out makes at least 6-7 nice sized pizzas (its more of a medium size) To roll it out all i did was keep my hand wet and smooth out the door, it was fast and actually fun to do! My husband loves it and I do as well, it cooks up great without any issues, and you can make a good couple pizzas- definitely great value and a good price. We went to the actual site and it was MUCH more expensive than amazon. the dough is alittle sticky, hence why you want to keep your hand wet when shaping the dough out for the pizza, you cook it about 6-7 mins before you put the ingredients on... HOWEVER if you do forget to cook it first alittle beforehand it really doesnt affect it much, my friend and I have both done this by accident a couple times but it still turned out good :P Its alot of pizza for your buck, How many pizza joints do you know that for 12 bucks you can get around 28 pizzas from? We will be buying more of this soon, Its great if you are doing a kids party and need alot of pizzas, like i said one bag usually makes for us 6 med sized pizzas. Overall i gotta give this product 5 stars!!

I recently was put on a gluten free diet, and it was difficult find a dough or flour that would make a decent tasting pizza dough.  Bob's Red Mill Gluten Free Pizza Crust Mix is wonderful!  It actually risees a bit, and has a chewy texture that is similar to regular pizza dough.  The taste is good as well.  I am glad I found this product.

Everyone ate this pizza as if nothing were different from regular pizza! (and I make a good scratch crust, if I do say so.) I threw some extra spices in the sauce to cover up any potential funny taste, but it wsn't needed! The edges of the crust were delicious, as well! The crust was even crispy on the botton thanks to the pre-cooking! Thank goodness we dont have to adjust our pizza eating now that we have a GF eater in the house!

column9: Finally! Great tasting, soft, chewy gluten free pizza crusts!
column10: These pizza crusts are wonderful. Each package makes 2-12 inch pizza crusts, or 4 personal size pizza crusts. They are great to prepare ahead and freeze, making for a wonderfully affordable fast and easy, gluten free meal. The only drawback of the packaging is that it's pretty difficult to try to make a single crust at a time.

column9: the best GF pizza crust and what a bargain!
column10: It's good! It isn't the same as a regular wheat crust but we'll never find that in a GF crust.  But it's good enough, and quite good compared to other GF crust mixes available today.  The package says it makes 2 12-inch pizzas or one slightly larger pizza.  The dough is sticky and you do have to pat it quite a bit to get it to spread out into two 12 inch pizzas.I made 6 small pizzas out of a batch and par-baked the crusts before freezing them. It's easy to thaw one out then top and bake.  I've also frozen the crusts with the topping when making a traditional tomato sauce and cheese pizza.  The plain par-baked crusts are handy for when I make non-traditional pizza.  My favorite toppings are things like goat cheese, sundried tomatoes, roasted garlic, fresh spinach, etc and they don't freeze as well.  I've not found any changes in the texture or flavor of the crust in the reheated pizza.GF pizza, both frozen or from a mix, are very expensive.  The Subscribe and Save deal is amazing!

I've tried a few gluten free pizza crust mixes and this is my favorite. Not only is it easy to make, one package makes two good sized pizzas. One of the things I miss eating since having to omit gluten from my diet is pizza and I really enjoy this crust.

column9: Love Bob's Red Mill GF Pizza Crust Mix
column10: The first time I made pizza from this mix, I used too small of a pan and the crust was really thick.  I was excited to have a thick crust pizza, but when I tasted it, I hated it.  I thought I had made a huge mistake buying this.  Then I decided to try it once more using a larger pan so that I had a very thin crust.  It was delicious!  I will definitely buy this again and again.

I made this crust into one medium size pizza which gave it a thick crust. When I did it this way, the crust was more like a biscuit than a traditional crust. Both my husband and I were quite happy with the results.

I am not allergic to gluten, I'm just a girl trying to eat healthier and I thought this tasted fine. I was afraid to try this after reading the reviews here, but it was actually pretty good, people who hated it must've cooked it wrong. It didn't rise as much as regular dough, but tasted pretty much the same. The only thing I will say, is that it suggested on the package to let it cook for 15 minutes, I found ten minutes was enough. However, we have a new oven. I also made a vegan version using Bob's Red Mill flax meal as a replacement for eggs, still delicious. Also if you have trouble rolling out the dough, it says ON THE PACKAGE, you need to push it around the pizza stone or dish with wet hands. Not exactly rocket science, people! Anyways it was yummy and  recommend it

This crust is easy to make and tastes good.  My non-gluten free friends don't mind eating it.  I add some oregano to the mix, which seems to go over well.  I don't remember what the instructions say, but I cook it first, then turn it over and put it back in with the toppings.  It makes two crusts.  If the 2nd crust isn't eaten right away, you must use/freeze it by the next day.  It doesn't have preservatives, so will mold quickly.

column9: a great gluten free pizza dough!
column10: When using this you should bake it for an extra 10 minutes before adding the toppings and another extra 10 minutes after the toppings. I really wanted to love this mix.  Our household has recently gone gluten free and previously we were making homemade pizza crust and focaccia on a regular basis.  What it really boils down to for me is taste.  This may have an acceptable texture, but the taste is terrible. I have tried it with a tomato base sauce and cheese, and because I have three mixes left...I guess I'll try something else.  Maybe a BBQ sauce pizza would drown the taste of the crust.  :-(  I don't want to throw it away but I'm thinking about it.  Really....I don't know how this got a good rating over all.  It tastes terrible.

column9: If you know how to make a pizza form scratch, this is great!
column10: Our first attempt came out very good, our secound attempt was fantastic.  We even had some friends come over and try the gluten free pizza, they all loved it.  The trick here seems you have to be a able to make a regular pizza first, if you know how to do that, you'll get the hang of this slightly more moist dough on the first or second try.  If you've never made pizza before, expect trouble...

I make up 4 crust at once, cook one and freeze three of them. They all taste great. I have also let the dough sit in the fridge for a day or two and we actually thought the final crust tasted better.

Here they sell them 2 for $2 ... can't believe the price I'm seeing on here.  They're awesome but not worth $3 a can even though they're large cans.

However, for fans of full-calorie beverages, I'd definitely recommend Arnold Palmer's Southern Style Sweet Tea with Pink Lemonade for a nice change of pace.  I marked it down a star because of the cost - the price of one can at the store was less than half the per-unit cost for this case.

Stonewall Kitchen's Mango Chutney is terrific. Chutney is a very under valued condiment in our American cuisine, too bad for those who don't use it to enhance even the simpliest of meals. It didn't arrive when expected, but when the company became aware of this they completely refunded my full purchase price very quickly.
