They really need to do something to add some more flavor. I was also surprised at the size of the bars. They are at least twice the size of the Quaker Oates Granola Bars. If they add a little honey and some more chocolate to these I would buy them over the others. As long as the price was the same or lower than the other bars. Another thing that would help the flavor would be to use salted nuts on them. Kinda like the Payday candy bar. The nuts on these are really blah and a little honey would help keep them stuck to the bar too.  I found one of these broke up and added to a bowl of ice cream is pretty good. And I like to freeze those pudding cup things, makes them like ice cream, and part of one of these bars broke up and mixed with the frozen pudding is pretty good too. Makes a different healthy snack food any who. Or closer to healthy than a lot of junk snack foods out there and makes them something different.

I was hoping for a more enjoyable product in several ways...The bars are on the small side at just over an ounce each and 140 calories.  The taste is marginally acceptable but reminds me of eating a slighlty bitter cocoa-flavored rice cake.  My biggest issue is with the consistency of "chewy".  If by chewy the manufacturer meant that when you eat it that it becomes stuck to your teeth than mission accomplished.I would recommend trying one of these before buying a case of 6 boxes (e.g. 42 bars).

I have to give these bars 3 stars as they have brown rice syrup as the sweetener.  I actually received these right after the news came out about brown rice syrup being a large source of arsenic in food. According to multiple sources, you should not eat more than one item per week that contains brown rice syrup so your body can process the arsenic. So you can make your own choice but I will be looking for other alternatives.

column9: Some People Like The Taste of Health
column10: For my review, I gave out these bars to for of my friends -- all males.  Three of these friends are healthy oriented, and they liked the bar.  One in fact is a vegetarian and loved it.  He commented how he was happy the bar didn't have an overwhelming 'oil smell' to it like other bars.  The other two that enjoyed it thought it delivered what they've come to expect from healthy food -- average taste but on par with healthy food taste.  And the fourth person who isn't used to eating healthy food, thought it tasted like crap.  No surprise since this person is more accustom to Oreo cookies than health bars.Personally, I thought the bar tasted just okay.  I was hoping for a more powerful cocoa taste but it's only a light flavor.  To help these bars along, I put a layer of peanut butter on them.  That bumps my rating of them up to a 4 out of 5.  :)  Honey might do the trick too.  I did find the texture and crunch to be at just the right level although I thought the bar could be a little more moist.These bars are definitely for the health conscious so don't expect a lot of flavor, but the flavor isn't unappealing -- it's just light.

All Natural Rich Cocoa Chewy Granola BarsPackaging is neutral and gives an earthy feel.  Upon opening, I see the words "EAT. THINK. Smile"  so let's see how I feel about each of those...Eat... As I open the package the appearance is like that of most granola bars.  You can see the rice crisps, oats nuts and cocoa bits.  The smell is a pleasant marshmallowy fragrance.  Taking a bite, well, I was not impressed with my first bite.  The bar is dry and actually very chewy seemingly like stale rice crisps glued together.  I did experience a strong cocoa flavor and spent a while chewing.Think...This experience is really making me think about the nutritional facts, so I look it over and I'm not very pleased with the fat, nor the carbs vs. proteins.  The fiber is ok but I can think of many other ways to get fiber in my diet. However, the sodium is a very nice low #!Smile....After a few more bites I have decided that my original choice makes me Smile and if I have nothing else to eat, I could eat one.  Otherwise, I am going to stick to my Kashi GOLEAN Bars which do have a higher sodium count and is a tad higher in fat.  But the taste is far better as well as all the other labeled nutrients like sugars vs. carbs and the vitamins....go look for yourself and see what you THINK!

column9: a great work horse bar that will give you energy, has a great mild flavor and you won't get sick of
column10: The Think Smile Cocoa bar is already my favorite bar!! It is hard not to grab for another after eating your first.  I have tried tons of bars:  Cliff (not too sweet but somewhat vitamin taste), Odwalla (soft but has somewhat vitamin taste), Nature granola (dry and hard- a relative of mine chipped their tooth on one), Luna (can be sweet but nice and light), Kind (great but pretty sweet almost like a desert- sometimes I can't finish it), Kashi (nuts can be rancid and many of the bars sweet), Trader Joe's breakfast bar (chewy and mild but okay taste- peanut is better than chocolate) and Larabar (cake like but for me a bit of after taste).I think what I love most about the Cocoa bar is that you can have a bunch and not feel sick of it.  Sometimes I have to eat 2-3 bars at work a day whenever I can because I don't know how my schedule will be and this bar always fits my mood because it doesn't have an overpowering taste or heaviness.  A lot of the energy bars and breakfast bars have a lot of sugar, feel heavy, taste like you are eating something with a vitamin taste or you just feel like you are eating something healthy and force yourself to finish it- ugh!I want something that tastes good and I can keep eating throughout the day.  My old standard was the Kashi peanut chewy bar because it is slightly sweet, not heavy and isn't really dry.  But unfortunately a lot of the time the peanuts are rancid.  The Think Smile Cocoa bar is, in my opinion a lot better.  It has a light feel (it contains rice crisps), a mild cocoa taste that isn't over powering, is chewy, not too dry and has a mild sweetness compared to other bars.  I won't say it is bland but if you like a bit of chocolate taste, this bar is perfect for you.  I even gave one to my mom and she is the pickiest eater ever and she wanted another bar....If you are looking for a great work horse bar that will give you energy, has a great mild flavor and you won't get sick of I highly recommend trying this one.  (I think they also have a berry one, I haven't tried that one yet!)

Title says it all...Someone mistook some asphalt for chocolate! Ew! These are hard as a rock and don't taste like chocolate at all!You get the granola taste sure, but again, it's so hard it's impossible to enjoy it.Skip it.

These granola snacks are very yummy with a good chocolatey flavor. They have really healthy ingredients with no corn syrup of any kind which I appreciate, and at 160 calories with 12% of your daily fiber you don't feel too bad about eating it. The only thing is you need about a gallon of water with it and you need to be ready to do a lot of chewing. I wouldn't recommend these for a quick refueling on a bike ride or hiking because you have limited water in those situations. But for a mid-afternoon snack at work they are fine and more nutritious than you would generally get.

From the moment you cut open the package, the cocoa smell wafts out, and you know you're in for a treat.  The Eat.Think.Smile. rich cocoa granola bar is delicious and healthy, a sometimes rare combination. It's easy to understand the ingredients and is easy to nibble on for a great quick breakfast or snack.The special African cocoa has antioxidants, according to the package, and is comparable to a cup of green tea, one of my favorite accompaniments.  The box and web site explain the details about how healthful cocoa is, and why its CocoaOne is so special and exactly where it comes from.  Each main ingredient in these bars, whole grain oats, rice, cocoa, and nuts, stands out nicely.  There is a lot of competition for granola bars, but this one is low in sugar and fat, though it isn't high in fiber, it does contain some, 3 grams per bar.There is crunch when you bite in, though an occasional piece may be a bit hard, you know you've got something substantive.  It's not sticky like some bars and doesn't crumble which makes it easy to eat on the go.  It comes in other flavors, which I have actually tried, and I'm impressed with the choices.  I'm think the name is too long and it would be better with just one word, instead of trying to be clever with  fanciful sayings. However, the product is tasty and hopefully, good for you. It's nice to see a company promoting a product for healthy living.

column9: I wish I could give it 10 stars!
column10: These are simply delicious.  No. Really. I have never enjoyed any health bars out there ever.  Usually they either are too sweet, too crunchy, bad aftertaste, no taste or too mushy.  Just can't please me. Till now.These bars are soft - but not mushy. They have a nice crunch to them without worrying about TMJ. The cocoa is delicious but not overboard.  They are not sweet to the point of sickly. And yet they are extremely tasty and even satisfying to where I can enjoy one early in the morning and be ready for a light lunch a few hours later without feeling starved or deprived.  I don't know if that was one of the benefits - but it is for me.I have enjoyed these bars so much that I am looking forward to trying out their other selections as well. I just love the fact that I know I am eating something healthy, but don't have to sacrific my taste buds or my teeth to enjoy it.

These bars are pretty filling and don't taste bad at all.The soy nuts, oats and rice add a lot of crunch to them.You can taste the chocolate throughout the bars.They aren't very sweet or moist.They are full of "good for you" ingredients and contain a decent amount of fiber per bar.Much healthier than many of the granola bars that taste like candy bars.We found them to be more satisfying to curb your hunger between meals, but less satisfying for a sweet tooth attack.While I don't reach for these things at all, my husband thinks they're perfect for traveling.  He has to eat something before taking his medicine and they fill the bill.I prefer the sweet and salty, chewy granola bars, even if they aren't as good for me.

When I first bit into one of these bars I was expecting it to taste very sweet, but it is not real sweet like a candy bar. It tastes good, but not super sweet, so if you like stuff that way, as I do, then this is the bar for you. Most bars like this have too much sugar, this does not. Could taste better with more sugar, but I think it is better just like it is.

I never before found a can that combines brown rice, per say, and beans. You heat it up and add some tasty choice of Beef, Fowl, Seafood or Veggies and you have a standard meal ready to be consumed. I have come to appreciate Eden Organic. Yes, I admit that I usually add a little more salt, pepper and herbs but in the end they do taste very good. I initially was looking for the beans alone but when I read the label and since I only use brown rice now a days, we gave this combination a shot and for us, it paid off! I can cook all manners of legumes, beans, etc but hey, if a nice organic company wants to do it for a while for an acceptable price, why not? For sure 4 Stars or even higher, they are reliable fare but for a couple of weird reasons we ended up with 6 cases of different kinds so we are still figuring how are we going to consume so much since most of the times we are only 2 people. That is the beauty of canned food, I guess, that it does keep longer and well. 4 Stars!

column9: i couldn't manage to choke this stuff down
column10: like one other reviewer, i'm from the "Deep South", so my regional culinary experiences have colored my perspective of what "rice and beans" should taste like.  still, i have a hard time imagining anyone finding this stuff even remotely palatable.what i like about it?  Eden is a really good brand.  it's organic, and it's got good ingredients and low sodium.what i don't like?  really, this stuff is pretty foul.  personally, i didn't think it smelled that bad, but the taste was another story.  the rice itself wasn't quite cooked to my liking...i prefer for my rice to come out a bit dry, and this was very different.  but over-moist rice i could live with.  there was nothing wrong with the beans themselves, either.  the biggest problem to me was the "sauce", for lack of a better way of putting it.  you know how when you buy plain, unseasoned canned beans they come canned along with this thick, gloopy juice-type liquid?  the "sauce" was essentially that stuff with a tiny bit of onion, garlic, and sea salt added, and it tastes every bit as bad as it looks as it oozes from canned beans when you drain them.  it almost makes me wonder...did they intend for people to drain the beans and rice before heating and eating?  if so, the can doesn't say.with a good deal of modification, this stuff might be edible, but i don't think there's anything that could be done to make it actually taste good.  i had picked up 1 can from Whole Foods to have for lunch at work, where i don't exactly have a good supply of seasonings on hand.  i ended up at the Greek place across the street instead, because i just couldn't make myself eat this.  based on what i'm seeing here, there are quite a few different varieties of "rice and beans" made by Eden.  perhaps some of the others are better.  in any case, if you're thinking of trying some, definitely DON'T start here!!  the pinto beans and rice are just awful!

I'm from the south. I'm no stranger to the rice and beans combo. This is one of the most foul things I have ever put in my mouth. It's not quite as bad as vomit, but it's close. Coming out of the can it smelled of rotten feet. I thought I'd give it a chance and heated it up. No luck. Now it tasted like hot rotten feet. Ketchup? Even worse. Maybe my dog will eat it.I honestly feel like throwing up right now.It is THAT bad.I don't know what in the name of holy hell kind of pinto beans or rice they used, but DAMN.EPIC FAIL

column9: The best olive oil you've never heard about before
column10: No joke. I wanted to start using olive oil for my family for health reasons but I honestly never understood why people liked it quite so much. It had...for lack of a better way to describe it...a strange aftertaste or taste on the back of my tongue that I found very unpleasant. I am very curious about food and always asked people about it...figuring it was entirely possible I hadn't had a good experience with olive oil. While vacationing in Florida I was in a Greek district (Tarpon Springs) and found a small Greek grocer who was extraordinarily kind. When we came to the olive oil section, he pointed out all the olive oils that were popular with tourists. My question to him was, "Which one do you have in your kitchen at home, though?" He pointed to this oil...the one with the peculiar logo was the one on his dinner table. I didn't try this until I got back home to Arkansas. In one teaspoon I was elated and crestfallen. I'd finally found a truly sweet, flavorful olive oil without the strange aftertaste. I now saw what people enjoyed and appreciated about this ingredient...and I live in B.F. Arkansas and finding it would likely be next to impossible..great. I started searching for it immediately. I found it on Amazon, but at the time they were out of stock. In my research, I found this is a farm who harvests and makes all the oil they can for their farm..then they are done until next season.  Well, that explained why it wasn't available at the time...and spoke to me about the commitment of this farm to only put out a quality product. I kept an eye out and once I found it was available again...I got a 3L can.  There are plenty of ingredients I can get just about anywhere. My olive oil is NOT one of those things. I am very picky. This olive oil is smooth, sweet and delicious. If that matters to you, this is the one to get. If not, buy whatever makes your tongue happy.
I could not find these peppers when I moved to a new area. I was so glad to find them on Amazon. These are the best roasted red peppers, ever. So flavorful and consistent quality every time.
I love this granola.  The best I have yet had.  It has a little kick to it and it full of my favorite nuts.  Great stuff.
My secret ingredient for soups, stews, meats, and any savory dish.  Now the same great flavor with NO salt!

This is excellent and very tasty, I use to use Goya Sazon still love it, but due to being on a mostly salt free diet have to buythe salt free version and this surpassed my expectations. It is the same as the Goya only without the salt, I live inMassachussetts and it is impossible to find salt free Sazon, thank god for Amazon.com or I'd never have gotten it, it is madewith the same ingredients as Goya, love it I will buy it again

This is a God sent as I love the flavor of Sazon but, haven't been able to use it anymore due to having to follow a low salt diet.  The name brand Sazon is high in sodium and also contains MSG.  The Marshall's Creek version has only the herbs and spices and, believe me, tastes the same as the name brand but without the saltiness.  I've already used it to make paella, beef stew, and chicken fricasse. It works well with so many savory dishes.  If you need to cut down on sodium you can still create delicious meals with Marshall's Creek Sazon and many other Marshall's Creek seasonings.  I also bought their Adobo seasoning and it's also terrific.  I highly recommend it.

Has a somewhat liquidy cream corn taste, but if you mix with hot tea or coffee with maybe honey or Agave nectar, it is drinkable! It has helped me in alertness, energy and overall well being. Who doesnt need that????It also helps ease my fibromyalgia pain a bit. :)

column9: How is this vegan if it has butter in it?
column10: Um, I'm looking for a good mushroom base that's vegan. This one is advertised as such, but the ingredients include butter. Huh?
i received my order in no time at all! also all the seeds germinated and now i have very nice plants in my garden
I love sorrel raw. These seeds are what they say they are. Mine are already growing. Cheap and shipped quick too. Thanks.

column9: Italian Tradition and Delicious Treat for All
column10: For those who haven't experienced torrone almond honey nougat candy, you are in for a treat. This Italian specialty confection is authentic and a product of Italy. Although it looks like it will be hard and/or sticky, it is miraculously soft. Each piece is sealed in foil for freshness and carefully packaged in a small box like a gift. There are eighteen tiny boxes per 6.35 ounce package. When I was a child, after eating the candy, I would keep the little boxes and use them to store special treasures. I have added a photograph to show the individual packaging for each piece of candy.Only 45 calories per piece and 3 grams of fat with only half a gram of saturated fat, as far as candy goes, this is surprisingly natural. The candy is loaded with toasted almonds and flavored with vanilla, orange or lemon.  A distinctive very thin white wafer coats the front and back of the rectangle providing a satisfying lightly crisp texture. Torrone has a short ingredient list with toasted almonds as the first on the list and chemical additives thankfully absent, so there are no artificial colors or preservatives.There is nothing else like this Italian confection.  It is usually reserved for holidays, and I know in my house it wouldn't feel like Christmas or Easter without it, although it is certainly wonderful year round.  Ferrara's torrone would make a lovely hostess gift or an unusual treat to tuck into a Christmas stocking.

i grew up with the la florentine version. i should have went with that product instead of 'settling' based on price. the nougat is not at all delicate. it is ultra chewy and bordering on hard. not at all soft as is la florentine. the wafer paper is also not delicate, rather it is thick and very noticeable.i did not care for the taste of any. first i ate the orange flavored without looking at the box. it seemed to me to be heavy handed and, i thought, tasted of lemon. i checked the box to see if it were lemon, no. the lemon too was heavy handed. the vanila was borderline ok on not being overwhelming. all were to me, too sweet and too sticky. more like eating taffy than the sensual and delicate la florentine i grew up with.i was disappointed as my wife had never had these before. it was a poor showing of what i had thought they should have been. i had to apologize to her after having raved about the tastes i had on my own. i rapidly canceled my subscription package.

We grew up with another brand and I decided to take the plunge with Ferrara and try it.  Upon opening the top (which is a lift up flap) the blue colored boxes were all lined up.  There are vanilla, orange and lemon flavors.  I tried the vanilla.  Opened the little box and inside was a sealed metallic bag which held the goody.  It was a good size, for Torrone, and upon the first bite the rice paper wafer was fresh, the nougat was sweet but not sickeningly and the almonds were toasted and crisp.  Then the childhood memories flooded in - I'm sitting at the long, dining table with the credenza behind me and I'm facing the front window looking out at a winter day. The women in the kitchen doing dishes and cleaning up after a huge meal, the Italian chatter ebbs and flows, the men watching the Christmas sports in the other room, and me sneaking the first tastes of Torrone enjoying bite after bite of the delicate goodness.  Memories in a box and this brand didn't fail.
I enjoy this candy so much.  My grandmother who was born in Ceafalu, Sicily used to eat this when I was a little girl.  It is really delicious, it is not real sweet but has a great flavor!
We used these to fill out the dessert table at my wedding.  My Italian family loved them!  They were moist and fresh!  We are thinking of ordering more for the holidays this year.

Very hard to find this candy down south.  My husband decided to buy a case!  We love this candy.  Very satisfying for just a small piece. Only 45 calories each too!  If you're a nougat and almond fan, I highly recommend this one!

These boxed little nougats take me back to my childhood in Pennsylvania. We would have them every Christmas. The candies are delicious and are now being enjoyed by my husband and adult children in current times.  It's never too late to enjoy a delicious memory or to start others on the road to creating them.  If you've been craving these thin wafery covered almond nougats from your past or want to try them as a new tasty treat, I'd recommend this brand with its individually sealed gems inside each tiny box that comprises the larger box.

Maybe it's because I'm used to better nougat but this one is not very good. The Vanilla one is OK at best, so is the Orange one but the Lemon one really isn't that good. You can find much better nougat (although more expensive) somewhere else like the Nougat de Provence by Roy René (amazon.com) which is MUCH better

Ferrara Torrone is my favorite and is a standout and way above the others that are on the market.  I have tried them all, but they can't compete.  I confess I am a torrone addict.  This deal is one of the best I have ever found.
This was a gift for my daughter and she loves this coffee.  Just wish it could be bought in stores in our area.  We can find decaf but not regular.  But, otherwise, great product.
so far the best gourmet coffee form Guatemala , and the prices is so cheaper if you compare whit other brands , fast delivery

column9: The BEST Giant Breed formula out there ...
column10: We have a 15 months old Blue Great Dane ... we still consider him as a puppy, even he is already 120 lbs. When we first got him at 10 weeks of age he was on Nutro Natural, but we switched him immediately to Eagle Pack, veterinarians and breeders pointed Eagle Pack as the shrpest formulated food for Giant Breeds.Since then we tried with Boston several other samples, from other brands. He seemed to like Nature's Choice Farm Stand Selects and Nutro Ultra food, but only for sampling. He's always happy to find a bowl full of Eagle there waiting for him to take of it.Regarding ingredients and supplements, Eagle Pack Super Premium is the far best of all. And the fact that it is specially balanced for Giant Breed dogs is something that You won't find anywhere else.Consider this food for Your Giant Breed best friend. Look at the labels, check the ingredients, read about protein balance and other stuff that your dog needs. I guarantee that You won;t find any other food that will come close to Eagle Pack. Let me now if I'm wrong. I will be happy to let Boston sample something else and than look at him when his all happy to go back to good ol' Eagle.Cheers !!!

Long time online shopper, but first time ever writing a review. We have a 7 month old Great Dane pup. When we got her at 12 weeks, the breeder had her eating Holistic Select Giant breed puppy food, which was good for awhile. Then her stool became very loose. So upon reading other reviews we switched to Eagle Pack Giant breed puppy food. Her stool was still a little loose, but we thought that it was possibly the switch of the foods so we wanted to give it a chance. Well after about 5-30lb. bags of eagle pack, her stool was still very loose and she was eating her and our other dogs poop. (very gross to be kissed by that....YUCK) A friend told us that she was doing that because she was missing a vitamin or supplement in her diet. She was also consuming a tremendous amount of food as well as always voraciously hungry. We started researching what to do then all of the sudden she was having uncontrollable diarrhea, not good for a 100lb. puppy. We did not have time for anymore research we had to do something now!We ended up at a local store and discovered Chicken Soup for the Puppy Lover's Soul Large Breed Puppy Dry Dog Food. We decided to try a a 18lb bag, even though the protein levels were a couple percentage points higher than we had been told to give a Great Dane. But the list of ingredients was wonderful when compared with a lot of other top brands, I am no expert but just reading the long list of ingredients it seemed that they had more all natural ingredients, as opposed to the supplements that the others were putting in their food.We got it home and immediately made a complete switch from the Eagle Pack food she was on. We did not do the customary blending of foods for a week or so to introduce the new food and ween her off the old. We did not have time as her tummy was so upset, we also did not want anymore of the Eagle Pack in her system. She loved the taste and gobbled it up. Within about 24 hours her poops started to firm up a bit. This got progressively better as the week went by, but still a little soft as to make picking up difficult especially on grass. We added In Clover Fresh Digest Daily Intestinal Aid for Dogs to her food and presto she pretty much has a firm stool every time, She is also eating noticeably less food (YAY!$$$) which she seams to be getting better nourishment from it. She is also no longer eating poop (YAY!!!). We attribute that the little bit extra protein in this food is what she was missing from her diet. We are going to ween her off the In Clover Fresh Digest Daily Intestinal Aid for Dogs and see how she does without the supplement now that she is totally use to her new food.To sum it up:1. Good quality ingredients2. Less supplements than some other brands3. Slightly higher protein than we would like, but it keeps her from eating poop so that is ok4. Affordable5. Retains more of the food so she eats less, which saves a fair amount of money.6. Her coat is super shiny and healthyP.S. We also switched our senior citizen American Bulldog to the Eagle Pack Adult food, and she got a very loose stool as well, and she has never been loose a day in her life. We now have her on Chicken Soup for the Dog Lover's Soul Large Breed Dry Dog Food, and she is great and very healthy as well.

I was really leery of spending $45 on dog food when we first ordered this for our 100 lb German Shepherd.  After being on it for about 4 month or more now I am convinced that it is worth the price for several reasons:  Our dog eats less of this food because of the higher protein content so a bag last a long time, his coat is shiny and he doesn't stink like our other dogs did.  That is what amazes me the most is that his breath isn't horrible like most dogs and that he doesn't stink at all!  I will continue to buy this for our dog as long as I am able!

Magnus my 6 month old English Mastiff has been eating this food since we brought him home and it has been wonderful for him. The ingredient list can't be beat especially for the price. He seems to like the taste as he gobbles it down each time he is served. He has not had any stomach or skin issues caused by this food.
I have a great dane with a very sensitive stomach. We have tried a lot of good quality dog food brands and this is one of the few that won't result in loose stools and bad gas.

I bought this food for my 2 german shepherd dogs after reading all the good reviews. Right after eating this food they both started itching and scratching like crazy! They also had very bad gas and were belching non stop. Needless to say the 3 of us did not get any sleep at all that night. There are way better foods out there for the same price, although just because it did not agree with my dogs does not mean it will not agree with yours. The ingredients in this food are way better than food you would find at wal mart though.
I was happy with the delivery time.  A little disapointed in the fragrance of the sticks.  I like to have them simmering in a pot to add a nice aroma to my home, there not as strong as i had hoped.

There's really no accounting for why cats, especially cats with kidney failure, will eat one food and not another, or will tolerate one food but not another.  That said, this food seems to be my kitty's favorite out of the prescription renal diets, maybe because the first ingredient is pork instead of some kind of grain.She keeps it down pretty well, too.  I also got her some of the chicken flavor, which has even lower protein and uses rice as its first ingredient.  She'll eat it, but she doesn't seem to like it as much as this one.She ate the Purina NF for about two weeks, then decided it was no good.  And I never could get her to eat the Hill's KD.  But this stuff she likes.

column9: Royal canin cat food renal lp24
column10: This is great for my cat she does not get sick or have soft poop.  The other brands don't work for her only this one I put out bowls of different food and she switch her self to this and won't eat the others.

column9: Not enough time for full evaluation.
column10: Our CKD Raskal did eat some, and the other 3 normal cats had some also. All we put out was eaten. Unfortunately Raskal was already stage 4 when we received it, and passed after only 2 small bowls so the remainder will be donated to a local shelter.

I bought this recently when Amazon had it on sale, ended up being around $6.00 a pound.  Not a bad price for an organic whole bean coffee.  Description says it finishes with a sweet marshmallow taste, I didn't find that to be true.  I would rate it as average, good coffee flavor, but not worth the regular price.
This is a smooth and fairly mild coffee that has very mild hints of coco berries and marshmallows (not overpowering, just a hint). It's my personal favorite. Love this coffee.

So, so good!  I ordered this pack of 3 a few months ago and it was Joyva Halva, just like I remembered.  I agree with the other poster that fresh deli stuff can be moister, but this is the kind I was raised on and like best.  It was really good.
I would love to talk to the people who manufacture this product. It was horrifying when I started eating the dried up mess and a tiny tooth appeared. I will never buy or eat the stuff again.

I bought three cans and they were all very dry and not enjoyable. I did not check the date, but I have had this product many times and would not buy this again. My local grocer sells them in bar shapes that are always moist.
The Halvah was delicious!! It was shipped very quickly! It was also very fresh tasting!!! I would highly recomend the vanilla halvah!

Eye Bought This Product On A Recommendation. However, Eye Cannot Seem To Get Past The Strange Taste Yet.  Eye Will Keep Using It To See If This Will Pass Or If Eye Will Acquire A Liking To It.  The Package States No Bitter Taste.  If It Is A Sweetener, Why Should There Be Any Bitter Taste?

If you are looking for a sweetener that is delicious in tea, Stevia can be used to sweeten hot or cold tea. You can almost say goodbye to regular sugars in your drinks once you get a taste for the Stevia powder.Unlike artificial sweeteners, Stevia is never bitter and won't leave a nasty aftertaste in your mouth. The packets are easy to carry with you and you may even notice you have less cravings for sugary foods.By using a low calorie (0 Calories) sweetener with only 1 gram of carbs, you will be ahead of the game. Every single time you use one packet of Stevia, you are using less sugar and you won't even miss it.~The Rebecca Review

A nutritionist recommended these to sweeten my coffee etc. as there are no negative after effects unlike artificial sweeteners.  Stevia is made from herb in South America. Japanese tea drinkers have been using stevia for years with no ill effects she said.  It's quite a bit sweeter than sugar, so you need less of it as a replacement.I like this brand and put two packets in my iced coffee every morning with almond milk and 1 T cocoa--it tastes like a coffee milk shake for only about 70 calories as the Stevia is calorie-free! The stevia makes it taste like an iced dessert drink and is a great, refreshing treat for the day.This multi-pack offer for this price is about 30% lower than what I can get NuStevia for locally.

column9: Not as great as I'd hoped
column10: They were discontinuing these at my local grocery store and after purchasing this... I can kind of see why. I know that this isn't going to be an eating experience akin to fresh or even frozen tuna steaks, but I expected a little more than this.Taste-wise, there's not a lot of mesquite flavor. This was more salty than anything else. It's not a horrible flavor, but when you compare it to some of the flavors that abound in the bagged/canned/ready-to-eat tuna market this just falls short. I've tasted far better.Texture-wise, my tuna was rather dry in texture. I wasn't expecting it to be like the tuna you cook up yourself, so this wasn't really a deal breaker for me. Bagged tuna is sort of a 50/50 type of thing as far as texture and dryness goes, although I did note that there was a substantial amount of water in the bag.Overall this is just one of those items that is just a disappointment. It's not bad enough to where you'd feed the remaining bags of tuna to the stray cats or chuck the rest of your meal in the trash, but it isn't good enough to where you can see yourself going out of your way to buy more of it in the future. I've got a couple more of these tuna steaks in different flavors, so I'll see if those are any different. I wouldn't say that you should avoid this, but it wasn't really something I'd recommend rushing out and buying either.

Tried this for the first time tonight and was really impressed.  I heated it for just 45 seconds and it was delicious.  Not too dry, low fat, high protien and could not find the words 'high frutose corn syrup' any where.This is great for my HCG diet. Wish they came without marinade as an option. I am very happy!

Por Kwan is the ONLY brand of chilli paste with holy basil leaves worth buying.  I get it at my local Asian markets for $1.59, but if I couldn't get it anywhere else, I would ABSOLUTELY pay the $3.75 price listed here. Other brands are not nearly as flavorful.  Por Kwan is concentrated flavor... POW!  Not just heat... the perfect melding of garlic, basil and chili... there's a depth to it that I can't describe.  Just try it!
If you love butter beans you are gonna want to marry these little guys. Give em a go in whatever recipe calls for them but watch out or the flavor they just might send your buds over the edge!
These are by far the best butter beans! My family loves them! They are also great for soups and stews!High;y recommend them and any of the other Glory products line.

The delivery was on time and produce was well packaged.  I was disappointed in the taste of the product though.  I'm trying to find the old blondies I used to make about 30 years ago and haven't been able to find that taste yet.

Love the product.  My mistake for ordering without knowing how many boxes were in the package.  This is $9+ for ONE box of the product which does contain 10 single packets inside. I assumed it was at least a multi-pack but it was not. Almost 3 times what I would pay in the grocery store.

column9: tasty - low cal - low carb - what's not to like?

The box mine came in look a little different than the box pictured here but appear to be the same product.They turned out to be pretty good. This has become really hard to find in the stores, so I was delighted to see it on Amazon.Love this tea. Has just enough spicy taste without being overbearing. The touch of vanilla adds a soothing quality too.
Went to six supermarkets in Boston one day trying to find these peppercorns for a recipe. So much easier to order them from this vendor! I will be doing this again!

column9: Yum! - but don't use too much!
column10: I'm not sure how much good a review of Szechuan peppercorns will do for anyone.  If you're looking for it on Amazon, then you probably know what you're getting.  I bought the 4-oz package, which was a huge amount of the product -- easily enough for a year in our house of once-per-week stir fry.  These were fairly priced, and had plenty of punch -- a little too much punch, in fact.  My favorite recipe for stir fried Szechuan chicken with ginger calls for a tablespoon of these.  The result was a meal that smelled wonderful, but all we could taste was the peppercorns.So if you're looking for that "spicy/numb" mouth-feel, these are what you're looking for.  You might want to dial the portions back a little, though.

I ordered this product since it was the cheapest per volume available on Amazon, but what I learned was that you get what you pay for.  The product I received had a high quantity, well over half of the pods, with seeds in them.  The seeds aren't terribly difficult to remove, but it is very time consuming.  I had read on line that you can just grind them in mrtar and pestle (recipe I was using wanted powdered Szechuan pepper) but the seed when broken have a texture roughly equivalent to sand.I was also disappointed with the flavor intensity, I don't know if this is a problem with this particular product or if descriptions were simply overblown, but I got very little flavor out of the ones I used and what I considered to be a level of 'numbing spice' that was not even worth mentioning. Disappointed

column9: Prefer the regular containers but they aren't on sale any more
column10: I would give 5 stars for the flavor,  I really do like this blend,  but wish they would just package it the way they used to instead of making me pay extra for something I actually don't want.I know that fewer and fewer people like this particular blend of nescafe,  because it's getting harder and harder to find.  I used to buy the regular containers in my supermarket,  but then they stopped stocking it.  Thank heavens for amazon, I thought,  and ordered it here. It's unfortunate,  because I like a heaped teaspoon of coffee but these packets only measure out to a regular teaspoon.  So essentially I want one and a half packets.  Which is just all wrong.  But I do love the flavor,  so I'm trying these packets and hope it works out.  Or better yet,  that they restock the original containers.  Nothing wrong with them!

Having tried all of the Taster's Choice single pack offerings, I would say that the Hazelnut is my favorite because I've always like hazelnut flavored coffees. I also like the VANILLA STICKS but don't find the flavor as intense as the hazelnut's. A flavored, brewed coffee has a more intense and better flavor and has a more effective caffeine jolt, but the Taster's Choice instant is good in its own right.One problem with these coffee packets is that adding too much water can dillute  the taste enough to produce a bland tasting hot beverage. Were I to drink these as my morning coffee, I'd need to make at least three cups to get me going.Mostly I drink these as an after nap cup of coffee at home or as a pick me up cup of coffee at work. It's just far too inconveniet to brew a single cup of coffee at work and have to fool with the cleanup. Heating a cup of water in the microwave only takes two minutes or less. Occasionally I'll make instant coffee on Saturday, the one day of the week I work in the A.M.Cons:1. I don't care for all the wasteful,extra packaging, and tearing open a single packet envelope while half awake in an unwelcome introduction to the day. Sometimes it's easier just to cut it open with scissors.2. I also am not crazy about the small serving size of individual cups. A jar of coffee would be much preferable, but for whatever reasons Nescafe has chosen to go the single serving route.Finally: I like Nescafe Taster's Choice Vanilla instant coffee and enjoy it as an occasional treat. You might also enjoy it if you don't mind instant coffee.

Then they switched to the larger canister and watered it down to where you needed a heaping teaspoon to make a decent cup of coffee. Now the ultimate insult - these little packages!  The coffee is still delicious. But it is very hard to find in the supermarkets and is way too expensive. Too bad Nescafe found a way to take a wonderful product and ruin it!  The taste gets 5 stars. Unfortunately - like other reviewers mentioned - this taste doesn't come in the old containers any longer. Otherwise, you are most likely to end up with a weak brew.Packaging: Not quite easy to open. I had to use teeth to make a dent in the stick. The single-serving size may not generate enough coffee for most coffee drinkers. There is a good chance of over-diluting. This is what happened to me first time I used it, compromising the taste. If you would like to drink more than 6oz of coffee, you will have to use 2-3 sticks. As a previous reviewer pointed out, this may be a quick pick-me-up shot in the afternoon.

column9: Why pay more for packaging we don't like!

To give some background, I'm an espresso geek.  I like my coffee bold, and strong, so trying to drink normal coffee (especially of the instant variety) is like giving a whiskey junkie a glass of Kahlua and milk.  So with that in mind, take note that my definition of "weak" may be very different from yours.  Anyway, let me start with my review.  Taster's Choice is meant to be made in 6oz portions.  I filled my standard sized 12oz (The Who!) coffee mug around 3/4 to the brim, so I may have over filled it a bit. (READ UPDATE BELOW)  That being said, Taster's Choice would only provide you a half-full mug of coffee if you followed their instructions properly.  The coffee tasted similar to what you would find at a cheap gas station.  It can only be described as similar to Crystal Light packets, in that your water doesn't exactly taste like Gatorade, but it surely doesn't taste like water either.  I tried adding a few tablespoons of flavored coffee creamer to see if it improved the taste, and it did in a big way.  The flavor was then similar to what you would receive out of those automated "cappuccino machines" that you would find in gas stations and breakrooms. (You know, the ones that tell you to only fill up the cup 3/4 of the way because the machine keeps flowing coffee even after you let go of the button?)  If you have ever tasted the "cappuccino" out of those machines, you'd know that it isn't anything like cappuccino, but it doesn't taste horrible.  It's drinkable, and has a sweet kick to it.Conclusion:I'm sure that using two packets would improve the flavor of a 3/4 full mug greatly, so I'm probably going to try that next time around and update my review. (READ UPDATE BELOW) I'm sure that some people would find this useful as a "fast food coffee".  It's not great, but it's not bad either, and it provides a little jolt for someone who doesn't have the time to brew a whole pot.*UPDATE*:  I have now tried it with two packets in 8 ounces of water, and it is MUCH better.  It now tastes like quite a bold flavorful coffee.  Highly recommend that you use two packets for each cup.

column9: Tastes Good and Can Easily Be Worked into a Decent Breakfast.
column10: I originally found out about Nutella from an internet article about some clueless woman in California who filed a class action suit because she bought whole hog into the advertising. The suit settled in April 2012 and the firm dropped the health claims in their advertising.  Coming from the generation who was told in television advertising that menthol cigarettes were soothing for your throat, I am amazed at the naivete claimed by the public.Anyway, I thought that the idea of a hazelnut (cobnut) cocoa spread sounded delicious and tried it.  Now I always keep a jar around. It doesn't need refrigeration although if it gets too hot the oil might settle out. In that case just give it a good stir.The important thing to remember is that moderation should be observed.  I enjoy at times having a breakfast of multigrain sandwich thins(100 calories), toasted for crunch, with two teaspoons of Nutella (67 calories)-- not the two tablespoons mentioned as a serving on the jar, an ounce of Nantucket Blend trail mix(160 calories) and six ounces of plain almond milk (60 calories). This easily holds me to lunchtime.  For fewer calories the trail mix can be replaced with fresh in season fruit. No doubts the ones among us who don't buy fruit then find it a week later decaying in the frig, will actually have some fresh fruit on hand.Tastes good and can easily be worked into a decent breakfast.

This tea smelled flat and only had a faint fragrance...it smelled like grocery store chopped tea leaves in bags.The taste of the tea was also disappointing. Letting it sit for 10 minutes in hot water was the only way to get any sort of tea flavor out of the leaves and the tea tasted flat and stale no matter how long it was brewed.My opinion is that the tea I got sat in a hot warehouse for a couple of years before it got to me and therefore had all the flavor and aroma cooked out of it.  I won't ever order Heavenly Tea again.

column9: Did I love the lobster or the ghee?
column10: This is my first pre-made ghee purchase after reading about it. I got this brand because of the price and the size given. It's big enough you'll be able to do some cooking with it without using half the container. As soon as I got it I had to try it. My first impressions.. it's a pale opaque yellow color and there are solids in it while as a whole it's runny enough to go off a spoon. The taste brought me back to eating lobster. Rich, flavorful and it made me forget about the little lumps of the solids in it at room temperature. It was so good it made me wonder what was better the lobster or being able to dunk it in the fresh made ghee the restaurant served. I heated some up for just ten seconds or so and all the grittiness disappeared and it turns into a bright, clear yellow state and the strength of the flavor seems to mellow out. Regular butter is extremely bland compared to this delicious stuff. I need to try the other brands out there to see if they're able to blend the consistency better at room temperature.

I used to do a lot of Indian cooking, and made my own ghee in those days.  I decided to try a pre-made one again for the convenience, and bought this.  It's not the best pre-made ghee I've ever had, but it was the least expensive option on amazon.com when I bought it, and it's perfectly fine for everyday use.  I mean, ghee is just clarified butter; it's hard to screw that up and make a really bad one!  In my opinion, this one has a particularly strong flavor, which is a plus since you need less of it, and that also makes it a good mixer for combining with other oils such as olive oil (half and half ghee and olive oil makes a good sauteing oil for vegetables).  Use a little of this and maybe some other oil to saute potatoes or a variety of things and get a great and different flavor.  You probably won't need to add any additional butter either.  Also, if you want to make your grains like rice extra-tasty, saute the dry, uncooked grains a bit first in ghee, before adding the water to finish cooking them.  It is worth trying that easy extra step!

column9: For proper Thai / Lao sticky rice.
column10: When I married a Thai in 1973 She brought this type of pot and five baskets to the states with her.  Neither of us expected to find these things in America but in those days we had to drive 100 miles to buy fish sauce.  Now Thai restaurants are everywhere, Thai food is in ordinary supermarkets and lots of people are learning to cook Thai.  Thais are learning to cook differently, too.  I've seen videos by Thais showing how to make sticky rice in the microwave or a rice steamer.  I've tried both, the microwave way several times, and the results were not like the sticky rice I have known for decades.  I bought myself a new pot and basket via Amazon and it works a charm.  I'm now again making sticky rice as it's supposed to be -- I am quite satisfied.  BTW I don't use any cloth.  The wife never did, I never saw such in Thailand when I was there and I'm doing fine without it.  Dropping the bottom of the basket into water to soak loosens any stuck rice but there's very little of that.  The wife brought five baskets because she knew they don't last like the pot.  Five was enough for years but they'd eventually come apart at the bottom.  I suppose a basket lasted us about a year or two.  We didn't eat sticky rice all the time.I consider this pot and basket to be required for proper Thai / Lao sticky rice.

This item is everything that I was hoping it would be.  I need a little more  practice in perfecting my rice making technique, though. All in all, it is what I was hoping for and expecting.  I would recommend these items to anyone interested in this item.
